New review (the first one can be found below) !
Okay guys, here we go again.
Dovetail released a beta-version of the game, and if you read the negative reviews (mine was as well), you'll get a pretty good view about what's wrong (at least until now) with the game.
I love simulators, I love hauling and I have found a love for trains. This game is a heavy haul train simulator, which means you will only haul goods, that's it. No people (except your colleague that sits next to you every game).
There, that is what you'll experience, coal and other goods that is moved up and down this iconic trail.
I love this game, have done since day one. I don't have a supercomputer to play with so my graphics are decent, sounds are great and in my ears sounds are realistic.
Simulatorwise it's great. You can push practically every button there is and they all have some function related to the game. You can move around the train cabin and outside, even leave the train by foot and let the lady run away from you (not recommended, but you can).
There are different scenarios to run, albeit a few but I guess there will be content for this later on. When you finish all the scenarios you have missions to do. I believe there is 9 for the old 38, 4400 has 16 and the mid train 12. So you'll never really run out of things to do.
I still wish there would be some twists to the scenarios and missions, some more random events happening so that you can't set the train in motion and go eat dinner for 30 minutes only to come back to .. well.. that nothing happened to the train.
Well, that's it I guess. I can today (after alllllll the fixes) recommend this to any train-loving player out there, even if you don't own a NASA computer. You will like it!
So, keep the DLC coming and please Dovetail, be open-minded about the scenarios and missions and the "randomness" of events :)
-----------------------------------------------------
First impressions (since I only played it for a total of 6 hours).
This is a cool simulator. Nice graphics and a great feeling in the game. I entered the game and started with the tutorials. Easy peasy, nothing more than learning how to start, stop and begin hauling.
Ok, that was the start, now let's get hauling!
I start off with the scenarios. Fairly easy. You start, ride and stop. That's it. I thought that the scenarios was going to be a bit special, maybe a sudden need to emergency stop, or a radio message comes in with a change in directions, a sudden snow storm or whatever. But nothing like that has occured yet.
Ok, so I started off a 2 hour mission/scenario. Hauled my goods to the end of the scenario. Run for 5 minutes along the train to the last car to unhook it and finish the scenario. Suddenly out of nowhere I derail.. screwing my mission up. Let me tell you, I didn't even move, I sat down in the seat and derailed... Allrighty I thought, no worries. Just reload and finish again. Well, the problem is; the save was right after my derailment.. So, 2 hours of game time and scenario down the drain.
Will I play that scenario again? Well, maybe in a long while.. Not that exciting.
So, I hope the other scenarios are more exciting or this will be a short lived game in my library.
Oh, and I surely hope they have SOME more DLC or whatever to look forward to, because this game is damn short without it.
I will ride a lot more and give a better review in due time.
Right now I can't recommend the game to anyone, and I surely hope that will change, we need a great train sim out here.
// Viking

Before I get into the bulk of this review, I want to address the elephant in the room, FPS. I will agree with what people say, the game is very badly optimised. This results in very low FPS most of the time. However, I have a mid-rangeish pc and I can run this game at max settings with 20-30 FPS. This might seem low but honestly for a simulator with this much detail its kind of to be expected. I would love to see a patch that increases the FPS, but I'm not to fussed about it. Also note it really depends on you computer, your results may and will vary. Now to get into the fun stuff.
First off this game is the best looking train simulator out there, this isn't much of a surprise seeing as it is made in unreal, but it is great to see what is possible. To further explain this, one of the major improvements over games like TS2017 is that everything is clickable. In the cab there is a whole ton of different buttons and switches that do what you would expect in a real train. This detail gives it the feel of what flight simulators have been like for years. The terrain is also great, around the track where you can see the detail close up, the texture work is great. Off in the distance looks okay but could do with some improvement because some times it can look a bit weird (I can't think of a word for it at the moment) but it is not terrible. The buildings in the towns are also a much higher resolution than old games, so they look much better. Overall this is a very pretty game and I don't see why people think it isn't.
Next topic is the feel and physics of the engines. From what I can tell the physics are pretty good, the trains feel heavy like they should and not just like tissue boxes on rails. I'm not sure how accurate it is but it does feel right, I have driven one of these engines in real life and what the game does is very accurate in my opinion. I have also heard that the physics have gotten much better since the beta. As for controls, they're very nice as well. The keyboard controls are similar if not the same to 2017 and still work. Actually clicking stuff is nice as well, you can either hover the retical over whatever you want to click and activate or right click the mouse to get the cursor and use that to click things. Over all the game feels very good.
The last big thing I am going to talk about is content. At the moment all you get is one (very long mind you) route called Sand Patch Grade, 3 engines (all are very different), Several tutorials (I'd say there needs to be more that go into more depth about all the different thinks in the locomotive), several different scenarios (all of which are very long and of varying difficulty level), and a free roam (there is a timetable where you can jump in and see different trains go by, jump on them to take a ride, and even take over control). I personally think all of this is well worth the price. It will keep you busy for a long time and I can't wait to do the rest of the scenarios. I'm sure more content will be added, I just hope it doesn't cost a fortune.
All in all I think Train Sim World:CSX Heavy Haul is a fantastic game that can use some improvements, but is definetly headed in the right direction. I can't wait to play more. I hope this all helped and didn't put you asleep with boredom. After all this I give the game a solid 7.5/10 mainly do to performance, but I will change that if they fix the problem.

I did the free explore one of the yards so far and built out just about all the engines. I was moving the last one - the one with the modern cab - onto the turntable to add it to the string of other engines I had built, when I went a little too far and ran it off the end of the turntable and that kicked me out of the cab. But it is so cool starting the older guys up. Two others were cold and dark and you have to open up the side panel, prime it, then crank while engaging the governor crank (not totally sure about that crank but they were starting). This is after setting breakers and isolating the generator, etc. It's very cool to wake these engines up!
So besides priming and cranking to wake the older engines up, you actually enter the turntable cab to swing it. It's easy though - unlock, swing as required, lock. But so cool to do. Everything auto-couples but it looks like you have to manually uncouple - or at least you can manually uncouple. The level of detail is amazing, too. Step lights, number lights, a lot more of the cab controls not only function but are necessary compared to TS, etc.
The two things that stood out to me was no slam or bang when coupling up. It needs the sound and shake instead of just stopping. And from me derailing the modern loco on the turntable, if there isn't a way of doing it that I haven't discovered, there needs to be a way to re-rail rolling stock and engines. Maybe it's there and I missed it. Will go back and see.
Anyway, it does need a good computer to run well if you want the eye candy. I'm sure it will get optimized some but with all it does to look beautiful, it might be worth people's while to look at the 10 series Nvidia cards to make this shine. 900 series cards and especially anything older are getting long in the tooth for modern sims that do all the stuff this one does.

Once again, the only "positive" or "negative" choice of review of steam don't allow me to really express what I felt about this game.
Stanley Parable is an interactive fiction with multiple "endings".More a special experience of storytelling than properly a game, Stanley Parable although really short offers a memorable experience.

Graphics are decent, it's of course something a bit outmoded, but the whole game is clean and acceptable.

If the music are just decent and probably forgetable, the voice acting of this game is what make it so special. The narrator is extremelly talented and never fail to bring you with him in the story. The second narrator appearing in one ending is also good even though she barely talk. Since the narration of this game is the most important feature of the game, it was really important that he was good.

The gameplay is really basic, you just walk through point A to point B, checking an ellement from time to time.
What is really important is that at every step of the way you have to make choices, they constitue the base of the game.

Just like I said the game is all about your choices, every choice lead to a different path and somthing like twenty endings. Every choice gives to the narrator the opportunity to react often in a comical way, making the impact of your choice even more important. Even if the game don't give any information, evolution of its two characters, it's the whole message behind the story that is important, the very meaning of the "adventure" of Stanley. Is everything real ? Am I in control of everything ? Why am I doing this ? The writting is clearly good but sadly everything can be done is about three hours (+ four for one of the ending).

Sadly, I wish I could say the game could be replayed as much as you want but it lose its impact on you when you discover all the ends, no surprise, no meaning in the disobedience since you know what is going to happen. I think it's really an unique experience that can really be felt once (or when you forgot about the whole game in years ?)

The Stanley Parable gives you 10 achievements particularly hard to get. If some are funny to get like "Clic on door 430 five times", some are really useless and annoying to get (even tho two of them can be achieve by changing the time on your computer) still it's particularly annoying for people that wants to collect achievements.

I will be honnest, no 12€ is not a good price for a three hours experience, no, 9.99€ is still not an honest price. The game is good but it honestly worth it's -75% price on sale or max 5€.
Please if you want to get it, WAIT FOR THE SALES, honestly buying it full price is a waste of money.

This game is a modern masterpiece. You fight bugs as a bug yourself. You explore dense damp caverns and elegant hallways. The thing that makes this game stand out above many others isn't the beautiful 2d hand crafted art, or the tight and comfortable controls, the sweet and poetic music, or even the lovable characters you come across throughout. What makes it stand out is the impact that everything has. You begin the game with an ordinary nail (your weapon) and a standard jump. As you progress you'll come across things that will help you upgrade yourself, combat and mobility-wise, but it doesn't feel cheap or easy. You work towards these things, and sometimes you won't even find that one upgrade you know you need to get to that one area until hours later. You pick it up and realize you have to backtrack all the way to the area you need it for, but it doesn't feel like a chore. There's enemies to occupy yourself with along the way, and you'll build up excitement as you have no idea what's behind that unbreakable wall or that high place that you previously couldn't get to. I've made it pretty obvious in this review that I really enjoy this game, but I do not recommend it if you aren't okay with backtracking a LOT because some people don't enjoy that and it ruins their experience. To beat the game my first time it took about 20 hours, but I'm still playing to get 100% because this game is just too good not to experience the whole thing.

Good game with a bit of potential. Generally speaking it has alot of same feel and functions that you would hope to play with in a basic colony builder. I found myself falling into the familiar - yet fun - routine of trying to sort out basic problems while optimising my little village(s). Where the game started to take off more me is in the exploration you find yourself doing on maps and the constant randomness of the maps you play on. Because of the constant change I feel like trying map after map so it gets high marks for replayability at this time.
Downsides at the moment - seeing as I'm reviewing this in early access - is that the 'end game' is pretty empty at this point. The few items like iron weapons and gold as an example are a nice perk for your warriors but certainly not necessary as you can just chug mead like a good viking and just have an uber army easily. The Kitchen - which  requires a solid amount of infrastructure to produce - is something that I enjoy from other games like Anno 2070 where you try to build up resources to have a cool pay off at the end. The problem is that at the moment this is one item - and it barely works even if you throw hordes of resources at it - which I found aggravating for an 'end game' item.
Game is a great deal of fun the first 8-10 hrs. - then I began to imagine how modding and an increase items and building to construct would really help the game. The gameplay is fun along the lines of Banished but without the community and fun items to build at the moment.
Would recommend - but it will need to be taken as a 8-10 hr. game in early access.

Stronghold Crusader 2 (SHC2) is a classic base builder/RTS. The only difference between it and similar titles like Starcraft or Dawn of War is SHC2's emphasis on economic and defensive buildings, as well as unit production.
In stead of simply mining for your bread, SHC2 has you grow the wheat with one building, turn the wheat into flour with another, and then has yet another building which turns your flour into bread.
This is pretty much the most decisively different feature that sets SHC2 apart from other similar RTS titles. Other than that, the game is all about right-click attacking with your troops. Look up some game play on youtube. Literally, what you see is what you get.

-Bread

-Balanced gameplay
Cons:

-Small number of interesting scenario-based missions

I get a WoW pvp vibe, with a mix of basic MOBA when I play this title. I have found myself unable to stop playing because even though the matches are short, I thrive to see what I can do in my next match to get better.
There are always a need for improvements. You have to change your battlerites to get that perfect build for a champion that is giving you trouble. Maybe you need more healing if you're squishy, maybe you need more offense if you're not having enough impact, etc. All the skills in the game feel like they are doing something, and every one of the champions are fun to play.
This game is not hard to learn by no means, but it is very difficult to master. I have learned a specific champ in my *8 hours of gameplay. I feel comfortable with that champion, but that does not mean that I do not play other champions. You'll always find yourself switching up to suit for your specific cravings or needs. That being said there are not very many champions, but there are enough to do us consumers for the amount of time.
In Battlerite, you will find yourself bored of the cosmetic skins, weapons, and mounts. Yes they are not all in your face flashy, but I'm sure in due time there will be better cosmetics to earn/buy.
On the end note. This game is very fun. I have not gotten bored (yet) of the gameplay with multiple maps and many new challenges to face. I see this game going very far during Early Access and beyond. I do not want to see another BLC mistake with this game.

RRE is a very good game - the physics and everything seem to be spot on, but I can't recommend it due to how the purchasing system works in combination with other factors which mean you don't get your money's worth. You'll have to spend well in advance of £50 to enjoy most of what this game has to offer and while that in itself is not much of an issue, the fact the server framework seems totally unreliable means you'll be sitting around twiddling your thumbs a lot of the time.
Sometimes the game won't work, sometimes it will. Your friend just down the road from you may be tearing his hair out because he can't get the game started after the latest patch, though it could be you doing the very same the following week while his game miraculously comes back to life. Throw in the Diablo III-style 'always connectedness' (where you simply have to be connected to their servers even for single player games) and what you have is a game that can be thoroughly frustrating.

updated 10/15/2015 after ~7 additional months...
This game is still in beta after 30 months from release date of February 2013!!
I am currently run the ADC pack, DTM 2014 pack and WTCC 2014 pack in RaceRoom beta.
Many improvements have been made in the past few months.  However, I still cannot give it a "thumbs up" recommendation at this time.
On the positive side the FWD cars in the WTCC 2014 pack are simply lovely to drive.  Good handling and excellent FFB make for a plenty of enjoyment taking these cars around any track.  The awful GUI is gone!
Items that need to be addressed by Sector3
Artificial Intelligence (AI) - AI is decent and quite clean by having good player detection coding.
AI aggressiveness needs to be added to game.
AI are "on the rails" when it comes to collisions - your car is not on the rails so if there is a collision between you and AI then you will likely spin out and the AI will continue running.
AI needs more options and settings to make them more realistic and less automated.
Business model - Having items and picks split between S3 store and STEAM is simply awful.  S3 needs to have all of the items available for sale grouped together.  S3 needs to dump the VRP and only list currency.
S3 servers - Having two sets of authentication (steam and S3 servers) is redundant and causes more issues for end user.  S3, dump your servers so players can still play RRRE if your servers are down, steam is down, or if players internet is down.
There appears to be no option to calibrate wheels and pedals in game.  My gear was recognized and works well.  However, I want to calibrate my pedals (set a small deadzone at start and set the travel of when I hit 100% of throttle or brake) and the game will not allow the user to do it.  S3 needs to add in a calibration function like the one used in iracing or rf2.
Overall, it appears to me as if S3 has been working on building out the available cars and tracks and only recently are starting to focus on adding in features and updating features already in the game.

The frame rate struggles at times. Some complain it is not a consistant 60 FPS, but it is a simulator, and does not require such FPS. Granted, smother is always better, but for a slow moving train simulator, super high FPS is not necessary IMO. I found the FPS to be very acceptable, and may improve with patches that address optimization. I run an i4770k CPU with a 980ti graphix card. There appeared to be no difference in FPS between High and Ultra setting in game, so I believe any bottleneck may be CPU bound.
Basically it is fun and relaxing, but if you are satisfied with Train Simulator, maybe don't bother, or wait for a sale.

Graphics 9/10

Physics 9/10

Audio 7/10
Locomotives and cars sound great, distant horns now sound much more accurate, open any door/window for more noise, ai trains sound great but do lack horns, more rail grind is needed in yards, coupling sounds are needed, - would love to hear a big bang when hooking up cars or pulling slack from train.
Playability 10/10
Switches switches switches!! I was hard pressed to find a switch in any of the locomotives that did not work, from variable wiper controls to loco/cab lighting, everything has been accurately covered in the finest of detail.
First person is a great addition, climbing/riding the engines and cars, operating turntables, starting/isolating lead or trailing units and being able to stretch your legs while in the cab keeps you busy on those slow sections.
Verdict: 9/10

The most accessible space building game yet.
I highly recommend this game to anyone who enjoys the theme of space. I've spent a few hours on this game with a friend of mine, she and I trecked through space in what could only be described as a "Miner's Life". Due to the game being far from complete, it is without question that methods of income are highly limited. The game begins you off with only a few blocks, the essentials for a hopeful star-merchant or space-hero, the basic thrusters, some cannons, a core for your ship, power supply blocks and some armors. Being a new-found space explorer, it is without question that chasing down pirates it THE stupidest thing you can attempt. ( Although it may be possible to successfully bring down a pirate at the start. )
Each system is a bit complex but it doesn't mean they are impossible for beginners to learn.
Power System suggestion: DO NOT CLUMP YOUR POWER SUPPLIES! It's ineffective.
The way the power supply works, I found it highly effective to line your system up in two 1 x X (X being any number you can afford ) lines that are spaced by one block each. So your systems would look like this:
-------------------------
-------------------------   Each dash being power blocks.
I'm not adept enough to figure out how the weapons systems work but from my research they're highly ineffective when clumped. I've seen a lot of suggestions stating that thirty cannon block separate and independent of each other are far more effective than all of them combined. Making bigger cannons practically useless.
Also included in this game is a crafting system which I have not personally tested, it allows for the mined raw materials to be crafted into processed variants.
Also worth noting: Each star CAN be approached. It's a matter of designing a ship that won't be obliterated by the time you reach it. Planets can be approached as well and even be built on to house a base or landing dock for the miners and would-be pirates.
There are still a lot of systems that are implemented that I haven't even touched. A lot being complex or lacking an updated guide. For example: Turret systems, boarding systems, in depth power supplies, and as I've said before, weapons sytems.
It is a game worth checking out and I highly suggest trying it with a friend.

If I had to summarize Valhalla Hills, I'd say it is Cultures, a game from 2000, with a lot less micromanagement, but sadly also loosing some of its depth. Valhalla Hills doesn't has a story-mode aside from the short story of being the cast out son of Odin who needs to build his way back to Valhalla. Instead, you play on randomly generated maps where you start at the foot of a mountain. You have to build a base and prepare your vikings to open a portal at the top of the mountain to advance to the next map. The units are vikings you cannot control directly. If you encounter a map you can't win or you don't want to play, you can simply generate a new map, but you loose the progress of the current one.
New buildings, biomes and stronger enemies are unlocked while playing by a kind of achievement system. On one side it gives the the game some progression and it doesn't bombard you with too much information, on the other side, the beginning is too easy and feels repetitive. It takes around 6-8 hours to unlock everything, but I hope the developer will add more content because it gets quite repetitive after 4 hours.
As I've mentioned above, the building part is quite nice, but the victory condition requires some more polish. After building the first few buildings to get building materials and food, you can assemble a little military force and start fighting your way through to the portal. the portal is usually guarded by several enemies that can either be killed, or you can sacrifice materials to bribe them. Sadly, the difficulty to produce these materials varies wildly. I had a few games in a row where I had to sacrifice water and plain old wood, very basic materials to bribe the strongest enemies. Other times I had to produce high quality products to bribe weak enemies, so fighting was much easier. The developer should put some more work into this ending to make it more satisfying for the player. Building a large and expensive monument could be a solution.
The mentioned fighting system isn't very fun either as it is partly luck. each unit does a fix value of damage to the enemy, but sadly you can't tell your units whom to fight first. The difference between winning and loosing a battle isn't preparation and tactics, but the luck of which enemy gets attacked by your stubborn vikings first, and if the enemies focus your vikings or if they spread their attacks over your units. Even worse: it can happen that a viking gets hungry on the way to war and wanders off to get food or sleep while the other are fighting. This makes fighting kind of luck based, something I don't really like in a building game. Some general orders for your vikings would be helpful.
The game uses the Unreal 4 engine to produce a good art style.The game is held in a cartoon style with exaggerated animations that can easily create the aquarium effect well known from games of the settler series or city-builder games. Sometimes you just want to take a moment and watch your vikings while they work... typically German, I know. The game looks especially nice during night time when all the different houses have torches in front of their door. The sound is good and fits the setting, yet nothing special.
All in all, Valhalla Hills show a lot of promise in it's early stage. It still needs a lot of work, but the team has a lot of knowledge in building games and a strong publisher covering their back. I look forward to seeing new content. If you like the genre, it is already worth a purchase.

I really .. REALLY .. wanted to like this game.
The original Space Hulk was the game that first brought me into the whole warhammer 40k world (that and the original role playing / skirmish rules). An insane future and hugely rich storyline.
But this game unfortunatley does not build upon any of that wonderful background.
It may be an honourable reworking of the original boardgame rules, but when you have so much more power and potential at your disposal simply trying to emulate a boardgame seems like a real waste of opportunity.
Problems :
The basic gui and interface is somewhat confuzing and I've often found myself wasting crucial movement / action points on needless turn arounds and minor positioning and placement. When it's really life and death between each round these positioning issues become very anoying. Some may say the game punishes you for being unattentive, but I kind of feel the game punishes you for not being pixel perfect in all your clicking.
The ammo for heavy weapons also is never enough and often I've found myself much rather having a standard trooper with a storm bolter then an assault canon (since bolters don't run out of ammo).
That said, bloody hell for all their high tech guns these guys use they sure friggen JAM a lot !!
I've had some missions end in minutes because every gun jammed everytime it was used.
I realise this is just rolling doubles, but I've played a lot of role playing games and rolled a LOT of dice in my time, and I don't ever recall rolling that many doubles !! Seriously programming guys, can you check your randomizers in your code 'cause I think you've forgotten to remove a rem statement or two.
A one on one battle between a marine and a stealer pretty much results in the loss of your trooper. Having a guy survive an attack is exhilerating but often short lived as usually in the very next round their gun jams and they die anyway.
I totally except this as the gene stealers are meant to be hugely deadly (read their description .. it's horrific), however their overall depiction in the game is more chibba-manga rather then 'holy crap this thing made my toughest guy crap his pants'.
They need to be made bigger and scarier, as from the overall look of the graphics it looks more like the marines should be wiping the slate with the dudes rather then this being a knife edge battle. Maybe too much time was spent animating the marines and too little on the stealers.
The space hulk graphics look great, but there is zero interaction with anything. This is an example of my 'missed opportunity' anoyance from above. Why not drop some fun extra's around the map and allow the marines to interact with the environment. As it stands the overall look at feel could be totally replaced by the tactical map as everything you see pretty much means nothing anyway.
Lastly some of the missions could be aimed more on holding key points and just having fun blasting wave after wave of stealers rather then pushing forward constantly. A real strength in the game should be your marines, but you never really get a chance to use their abilities as your constantly on the backfoot no matter what. Why not drop in a couple fun rounds which just play on the 'theme' rather then being totally based on the 'strategy'.
Good bits :
Killing wave after wave of stealers during those few instances when the guns aren't jamming.
That never gets old.
Marines .. look .. AWESOME
Winning is rewarding.
It should be made much clearer that your not only trying to beat the stealers but also fate itself as the dice play a critical part in the overall outcome of the game. Beating BOTH of these is awesome and keeps the game flowing.
Overall I think the metacritic score is harsh, but it is also fair.

It should have been more accomodating to new players and contain more of the huge and awesome background of the 40k universe. This to me is a huge oversite.

I was pleasantly surprised by The Bridge. The controls are very simple, but the puzzles get quite tricky.
On a gamepad, the left stick controls your character while the triggers rotate the world. That combines with physics and perspective tricks to make for some good challenges. You may need to rotate a level enough to get around to one side, but while making sure a key doesn't fall off of the level from its precarious perch.
The controls for the character feel very slow, which I would usually hate, but I think that the ability to rewind when experimenting made up for the sluggish controls.
I thought that the difficulty level personally was a really satisfying curve that kept each puzzle feeling like an accomplishment without getting too hard...until the last level; I had to actually look up that single solution. My girlfriend watched and helped with some puzzles, so it only took about 2 hours or so to complete the main game.
You should buy this on sale.

Edit after a year or so. This sim just keeps getting better. The latest release with the fantastic nordschleife really puts this at the top of the racing hill. They also worked out a few bugs that were sometimes interrupting the fun - no more. What was previously a great game with issues is now starting to really get polished. There is no better sim racing experience that getting into a good online race with this game. Shell out the $20 for some paid content, join some big-boy races with respectful racers, and never look back. The pricing model works well for me because i can buy once (still cheaper than the other sim) and not worry about a subscription. Again, no other racing sim gets my adrenalin flowing like this one - it really conveys the feel of speed and competition. Single player is quite good as well especially for European racing fans, but i'm more of a multiplayer user. Again if you are a sim racer and have not tried this in the last year, do yourself a favor and try it again - then judge for yourself. Even using the free content to get a taste should convince most.
There is still the odd bug or two, but the devs pay attention and always take care of the issues that the community brings up - for instance - currently player names above the cars are located off screen for triple monitor users. I believe this is about to be fixed in the next patch (as of 6/13/16), along with taking care of those with low ping to not ruin races. Check out the forums here
Final thoughts - at 450 hours played, i really should be faster! But i'm getting there....

*REVIEW FOR DAYZ MOD OF THE GAME!*
The game has never been perfent but unfortunatly the game is being downgraded each "update", If you are planing to but the game for ridiculous base building and giant helicopters flying around everywhere sure play for Epoch or Overpoch as they are essentially a seperate game but for the people who want to experience the true vanilla dayz, sorry you missed the golden times. Dayz was nearly perfect with the exeption of cheaters and glitches , the game was simply amazing, exploring the unknown world of Chernarus and encountering many people on the way and finding supplies was like nothing i have ever played before but the current state of the game although fixing lots of glitches and removing most cheaters, it is slowly bringing out some very useless anoyances to the game each update. These are some of the things that ruin the Dayz experience for me personally:
1. Blood Bags: Before around 1.8.2 blood bags were simple, it is one of the only ways to regenerate health and in its former state was great, no one had a problem with them but the new developers of the mod are wanting to make the game like the standalone by adding un-fun, un-nessecary procedures to actually use them. Something as simple as regenerating health has become a tedious process first having to find your blood type then finding the correct blood bag for your friend to use an external blood transfusion kit.
2.Zombies: Zombies are what make Dayz a "zombie survival game" and most people did complain about the easiness to simply out run them then hide in a bush making gunplay againsed zombies a very impractical thing, the response from the developers was to buff the zombies hit damage and numbers but let me explain something, zombies are NOT the main enemy, they are a simple fill in for all the empty of towns and the last thing you should do is to make it so that getting hit by them has worse consequences, especially when they have extremely laggy and glitchy movement and they spot players very easily even when sneaking. Players often die during essential activities like gunfights or looting because of zombies glitching and teleporting in infinite numbers to unfairly opppose a certain player.
3. Clunkiness: An unchanged, unfixed control and animation system has been used in Dayz since the begining with unintuitive scroll wheel mechanics and the slow animations of every actions which seemingly don't get cancelled unless you use the annoying scroll wheel... But this can be overlooked for more expirienced players, what cant is the new fatique system implimenting an awquard screen tilt/sway movement in mostly random times which in first person is quite nauseous and completly disabled players to properly use iron/aim sights.
4. Food/Drink: In more recent updates food and drinks have been made unnessecarily more difficult, from a full can of soda realisticly replenishing your health in earlier versions of the game now only replenish less than a quarter making those dire situations of starvation, looking for just one can of beans over 4 times more difficult.
5.Infection: Sepsis was not the best inplementation but quite a realistic intresting mechanic, altough quite luck based, it wasn't so common that you would find yourself dying of it often. This may seem good on paper but really isn't great when it is so easy to get infected from an over powered zombie hit or a blood tranfusion then easiely unknowingly being able to transmit from player to player.
6:Bases/Fences?: Ok this isn't epoch so why can i see clusters of big structures placed around the map, this ruines the immersion of the gritty survival game when there are little safe boxes people hide in. If people wanna build, trade and things unrelated to Dayz, they would play Epoch but if they want to explore and survive and PVP they play Dayz.
7: Crafting: You add useless items in the game littered around the map to be colected by players just for them to realise that you need to find 5 other useless items just so they are combined to be another useless item on the crafting menu. (Useless+Useless+Useless=Useless) this just adds junk to the game and wastes a potentially good crafting system using items that the player already has and can use.
I miss the unique Dayz game. The lag, glitches, zombies, controls etc, from the early versions are true issues but for every slight fix they sneak in new ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t that no one really wants just to further clutter and lag the game. Even with this it is still enjoyable (more than most other survival games) and it recommend it but not as much as i would have 2-3 years ago.

Ok....I just bought this game with the mind-set that it's going to suck and I am going to get a refund, honestly I wouldn't have bought this game weren't it for steam's refund policy. That being said, as you can see, I did not return the game, infact as soon as I started playing I didn't stop for 13 hours. Not ever have I spent 13 hours on one game, in the course of 1 day, not even that, half a day. If I had the whole day it would have been 24 hours. Alright, so let me tell you how I first saw the game. The graphics are crappy, the npcs are horrible, the tutorial is buggy and crap, the chat system is bad and the ui feels like that of a prototype. Notice thats how I first saw it. In all seriousness the tutorial really isn't good, I actually reccomend you don't play it and instead you watch youtube videos to learn what to do, thats what I did. Anyway, I was damn near convinced that this game was just a minecraft mod made into a game....untill I joined a server that is. I have no idea why or how but when you build your first crappy ship, and fly it a little bit and learn a little more, fix the crap of your ship little by little. Finally find a planet, land on it, start colonizing it, build another ship, learn about jump drives, learn about weapons and shields and cloaking devices and credits and so much more, the game opens up into this vast universe of many many many things to do, and did I mention there were factions. Basicly, if you like minecraft, or space engineers, or star citizen, or eve, or star trek, or star wars or sci fi in general, you will like this game. The only thing of any concern, is that this game's learning curve is steap, very steap. But trust me if you stick to it, gruel through the unknown of learning the game, you will find somthing worth alot more then 10$. Also, I have just played 1 game for 13 hours straight so I am tired and this review might be a bit excentric, but no matter. This game is amazing and I only see it getting better. Lemme start off with saying that if you don't have a numpad on your keyboard/have a pc keyboard or a controller, don't bother getting this game. At all. You're gonna have a haaaaaard time playing this game with it's immovable camera (pressing tab to reset your view does not count).

Wonky controls.... WONKY CONTROLS. My biggest pet peeve. The game was something I sought out after for the story alone, and many had already warned me I was better off getting it on the psp than on the computer but I went and got it anyway. Lo and behold, you'll have a tough time getting used to the keyboard controls. Having a controller REALLY makes it easier.
PSP-ish elements are still in the game, namely the lack of cut scenes and blank screen dialogues, inconsistent textures, short battles which are a waste for (what I personally consider) the game's battle system. There's also the issue of the game's resolution which was a problem on my end trying to start the game up and the lower fps (which I honestly don't mind, but I know a lot of people prefer a solid 60 fps or something).

The characters on the other hand... the strong stereotypes each of the twelve...thirteen... FOURTEEN playable characters (Not counting the badass summons) were... annoying haha, but fine, they're adorable in their own respect.

TL;DR: Not bad. Recommended for medium-high to high end computers.
Full review:
Is it perfect? No. There are bugs and performance optimizations that I'm sure can be made.
Is it everything I hoped for and then some? No.
Is it what i expected for a first release? Heck yeah! (and I mean that in a good way)
The first release of TSW has certainly come a long way since the beta. It has definitely been optimized quite a bit more and (obviously) theres quite a few more features. A lot of reviews I'm seeing complain about performance. Well DUH! It's running on U4. Anyone with half a brain knows that U4 is a very intensive engine that will beat even the most powerful of computers into submission. I'm running most of the settings in the high range and backed a few down to the medium range. I think it still looks pretty good.
There are a few bugs, as with any first release, but I haven't found any that are game-breaking or make it unplayable. I wish there was a way to hook together your own consist in the yard and take it across the route. This is currently not possible but who knows what the future holds. I imagine we'll have to wait for a scenario editor for something like that. The tutorials are somewhat lacking. I actually have the real world manuals of each locomotive so it was easy to translate that into TSW for myself but newer users may have some problems. That being said, I'm impressed with the level of detail the designers put into TSW. There are a lot of features that are on the actual locos that I would have never expected in a simulator.
In a time where developers will just release whatever garbage they can sling out it's refreshing to see that Dovetail took their time with this one and made it into something special. There is an absolutely ENORMOUS amout of potential in the new TSW engine and system. I can't help but wonder what the future holds for it. My mind immediately goes to the SEPTA R2 in Philadelphia or the Chunnel trains in europe. If this is the future of Train Sim then I'm full of anticipation.
Kudos to the TSW Team! You've started something wonderful.

Yep, aware this game is almost 3 years old:)) But I'm gonna write a review anyway! Dungeon Defenders is a choice game:) Recommend? Certainly yes. The following is a list of what I consider pros, cons, and things I am on the fence about . Pros being things i liked (of course), cons being things that annoy me, and 'on the fence' being things that are kinda  'hmmm...yeah, mehh' but not enough to sway my opinion of the game. And yes, my opinion is subjective:) Here we go:
Pros:
* Multiple characters to choose from with distinct abilities. Allows for a variety of play styles. You'll find a character who has a play style that you like and feel 'at home' with.
* Frequent character 'level ups'. Creates a good sense of character progression and hey,  we all love becoming more awesome:)
*'Level Ups' are well balanced. 'Level ups' on both equipment and characters feel like they are a real choice that impacts your play. But not game changing enough that you 'gimp' your characters with one poor choice.
* Insane number of loot drops. Even with multiple characters, no one is ever stuck for equipment.
*Four player co-op...c'mon, who doesn't love that?!!
*Local split-screen co-op.  Local co-op is a feature that is missing from way too many game nowadays. Its awesome to have this feature available.
*Levels have a nice varitey of design layouts, encouraging you to employ different strategies. You'll find tactics that work for you no matter what level you are on, but you don't feel like you do the exact same thing for every level.
* Awesome amount of DLC for those who want to keep the game going a bit longer:)
*Being able to change which of your characters you use ingame enables you to play solo if you want to, and you never feel like you are stuck without the defenses you might need.
*Controller support. Having a choice to use controller or keyboard and mouse is great. Both have strong groups of supporters, and its great to have the option that suits your preference.
Cons:
* Rather 'busy' visuals. Hellooo cataracts:)) (kidding). But, the very bright colors, and numbers and icons that constantly appear on screen can be a bit much on the eyes for some. I got used to it, but at first i wasn't sure i ever would.
* enemies have variety, but they lack character. It's hard to pinpoint why i feel this way, because I think it stems from a combination of things.  I hesitate to compare games in a review, but the humorous commentary and cocky swagger of the orcs in Orcs Must Die [by Robot Entertainment] gave the enemies a degree of life that is missing from the enemies in Dungeon Defenders. Also, the slower pacing of the enemies can make you feel like they don't have a sense of urgency. I never really felt that they wanted to destroy that crystal more than anything else in the world.
On the fence:
* Kinda slow pacing. I know I brought up the pacing thing in the cons regarding enemy character, but this element of the pacing regards a different aspect of the game. Everything, from your character to the enemies, seems to plod along quite dreamily. For new players, this can be great, so you have time to react. For more experienced gamers it can be a little frustrating at times.  I can imagine some people dumping loads of 'level up' points into their character just to get him or her to run around a little faster:)
* Local co-op players share loot and currency. For some, its a true chance to cooperate, or it creates a friendly rivalry for cash, and for others a frustrating race to see who can spend the cash to level up weapons and armor first. It depends on who you play with:)) Choose your allies wisely:)
* Story line is almost nonexistent and ultimately irrelevent. Yeah, if you want the story to pull you in and care about the ingame world and the related characters, this game is not for you.
* Cartoony artstyle. Sometimes i like it and other times i wish it was a bit more...mature.
There we go, thats it. These are my thoughts on Dungeon Defenders. So, if after all these years you are still having trouble deciding whether you want to play it...I hope this review helps.
Cheers!

In the future there is only WAR!  Welcome to the realm of Warhammer 40K.  Space Hulk was originally a board game based in this universe, and now it is getting a proper port-to-PC treatment thanks to developer Full Control. While it is not this IP’s first attempt to be brought to life via video game format, it is by far, hands down, the best effort any developer has ever put towards doing it justice.  Games Workshop is known world wide for it’s board, card, and miniature style games, so this really is a great IP for any developer to work with.
With the soon to be released Space Wolves DLC, now is the perfect time to invest in this game.  I know the cost tends to throw some people off, but you have to keep in mind that this is a board game, and if you went to the store to buy the board game, you would spend $99.99 USD.  Then you would have to put together each model, paint each model, and then after you got all of that done, you would still have to find a buddy to come over to the house to play it with you!  Full Control enables you to play with anyone in the world at your own pace, without having to set the board up each time you want to play.  So if you think about it in that context, the $29.99 USD price is a bargain!
30 Second Review
+ Ongoing and continued developer support.  Daily interaction with the player base.

---------- original review -------------
Reviewing: v.0.10.16 (August 29th)
Genre: Settlers meet Facebook.
I'm a huge fan of these kind of strategy games since the late 1980s. When people remember the good old days they tend to forget how shallow most games were back then. Modern games like Anno 2070 are the exact opposite, overladen with depth at the cost of sheer fun. If a single map takes 4-5 hours to finish that's not an achievement, it's a sign of bad game design in my opinion.
The challenge is to hit the sweet spot between intuitive fun and complexity.
"Valhalla Hills" is still in early access which shouldn't be forgotten here. In its current incarnation it leans heavily towards simplicity. A little too much for my taste. The progression is slooooooow almost to the point where I feel a little insulted. Not a big deal though because you'll eventually unlock the more complex production chains.
The real problem right now are the utterly missing feedback tools. There is a statistic screen that doesn't really help though. Example: You start a level and have 10 vikings right away. No one tells you what is needed to satisfy their demands. NOTHING! You're probably going to build some huts to give them a place to sleep. Some food production to feed them. Hmm... so you're producing 5 fish. What exactly does that mean? Is 1 viking eating 1 fish per time unit? If so, why are the fish simply being stored in the fishery and not being consumed? Somehow my vikings are feasting on berries they collect without having a berry collecting building.
Please give us analytical tools so we can understand wtf is going on!
The positives:
- Visuals are absolutely stunning, pros at work!
- Had no ctd yet
- smooth gameplay
- overall very professional feel
- devs used to work on "The Settlers 2" which makes me confident of things to come
The neutrals:
- no a.i. opponents => you can/will play at your own pace which can be both positive or negative depending on your personal taste. Nobody ever complained about that in city builders for example. I would prefer having other tribes nearby with whom you can trade or fight. Would be intriguing if you need resource they have a monopoly on. Choice: trade for it or fight over it. Unfortunately I don't suppose it will be implemented.
The cons:
- too shallow right now
- difficult to assess cause and effect due to lack of analytical tools
- forgettable music, mediocre sound effects
- no cohesive campaign yet. That was a bad surprise. In the main menu you can only select to play a new map which then is randomly created. The progression only consists of unlocking new stuff. I was expecting a campaign map with scenarios attached to each other. This needs to be implemented!!!
Conclusion:
Lot of work to be done. The technical foundation is extremely good so there's hope. The devs can purely focus on improving gameplay instead of having to deal with technical issues.
I can only give a moderate recommendation at this point. Only bought it because it was on sale for 16 Euro and I trust the developers' skills and dedication. Wouldn't have bought it for 20 bucks.
Rating for the tested version: 6/10
Will update this review. Will increase the score if the devs meet expectations and lower to a thumbs down if not.

Black Flag is a very fun game. More than the sum of its parts, it does everything in the "good" range:
Stealth and assassination? Good, some of my favourite missions in the series are in this game, but none are overly complex, elaborate, or ingenius like in previous titles.
Piracy? Good, I suppose... you plunder ships, dig up treasure, but you don't really care about the crew, easily replacable, no morale or use for rum other than selling. The violence has that "PG" feel that Pirates of the Caribbean had. As far as pirate activities go, it's held back a bit.
Ship battles? Very fun, but also a little arcade-y, I honestly preferred the ship battles in AC3, oddly enough, more weight and reload time to the guns, more sense of power.
Assassin's Creed franchise trademark "WTF" moments? Yes, actually. Good plot twists and ideas? Sure, but I wouldn't say it's groundbreaking. By the end though, it does feel more like an AC game than a pirate game, so it does bring it back around in comparison to the beginning.
All in all, I still say it's great, because what it does have is character, and characters. A lot of them, actually. And it does a decent job at keeping them unique, a lot of great pirates and villains, betrayal and crazy ones. They don't shy from killing off characters, as it does strive to be historically accurate with most of them. I really enjoyed it as it went on, and by the end, (minor spoilers, will be vague: ) found it very moving, overall, particularly one scene at the end [spoilers]where Edward sees everyone that's died (do you really think pirates lived very long?) and remembers the old days for one last time.[/spoilers] Similar to the ending in AC3 in a way.
If you like AC at all, and want an easy, arcade-like ship battle, that's basically what this is. You don't need previous AC knowledge. It's a very long, but well-paced and decently-written game, with good characters, controls, great visuals and progression, gameplay, etc. A solid title, IMO. Just sucks you need uPlay.

Let me start off by saying I was never interested in the Assassin's Creed series when they started to come out.  I saw friends playing the early games and thought "Eh not for me." And I felt the same way when Black Flag came out.  Ah, just another Assassin's Creed I thought.  Then I went to a friend's house and saw him playing around on his ship.  He explained to me how his crew could sing sea shanties, collected treasure, and you could customize your ship.  He let me play the game a bit, and I instantly got hooked.
I purchased the game, played all the way through it, got nearly every achievement, upgraded everything to the max, and I'm thrilled and happy that I did.
What I love about this game more than anything, is that a player who has NO IDEA what's going on with Assassin's Creed, like the different factions and what they stand for, and basically everything leading up to it, is completely fine to play this game because the main character is just like you.  He doesn't know what's going on, and he finds out as YOU find out.
If this game was filled with "Oh you should've played the second game to understand what they are talking about here" or "This won't make any sense unless you played the sequel to this other game in the franchise"  I would've hated it.  Instead, you follow along and discover what the game is about as the main character does.  It's fantastic, absolutely.
I found myself sailing in my ship at the slowest speed in calm waters at night with a full moon on the horizon as the crew sings a song, mourning over a lover who's died and was seen in their dreams.  It's peaceful, it's beautiful, and the enviornment is stunning.
I often tell myself, I wish I could forget everything this game ever was so I could replay it and experience it for the first time all over again.  If you have any doubts, set them all aside and just play this game.  If you love pirates, a wonderful story, and an escape from reality at home, this is the perfect game for you.

This game provides an interesting concept, but sadly falls short
Zup! 5 is a 2D puzzle game in which you cause red colored blocks or balls to explode, to propel your ball to a patch of teal on the level. The game's puzzles are simple, and so is the gameplay, but I feel that there is something missing from the experience. Whether it is due to the content or difficulty not ramping up I cannot tell you, but my experience felt very samey after only a half an hour or so. This doesn't mean the game isn't fun, but more content or features would be appreciated. The puzzles also are not very difficult, and only a few gave me trouble, mostly due to a puzzle requiring trial and error to complete, but nothing feels quite like sitting back, thinking of a plan, and then executing on that and watching all the pieces come together.
Some of the gameplay features seem to not make sense, the main thing that comes to mind is once the level is complete, a door just opens to the side and you click on it. It shows a strange disconnect from the gameplay, and I wish it was a different transition, and more tied into the gameplay.
The art is solid, but nothing above average. The minimalistic art style serves the game well but isn't an outstanding feature. I do appreciate the variety of color, and it does give me something nice to look at during the levels. The sound effects are also passable if a bit basic, things like the explosion when you cause a block to explode seemed a bit like a stock sound effect. the music was quite good, but the lack of tracks made it a bit repetitive, and I found myself wishing there were more tracks, as they were all good.
Overall this was a decent puzzle game, but I think it would be better suited on a browser a few years ago if you think it might be for you then surely check it out. however, the basic gameplay and mediocre art causes this game to fall right in the middle at a 5 out of 10 with a label of "needs more".

This sim is one of my favorites.
Since Sector 3 Studios was born, RaceRoom has received new force feedback, which is acclaimed to be amongst the best. New content has received new physics for cars and new more detailed track surfaces. Also, they are going through all of the old content and updating the cars to the new physics model. Most tracks have now been updated aswell, however they may have finished by the time you read this.
Combine these 3 things with genre leading sounds and you have one of the best experiences available in sim racing today.
Multiplayer has a unique style of netcode where your ping to each other racer seems to be p2p rather than via the server you are racing on, which is great. Racing standards in most lobbies I have been in is of a good standard.
Along side the DLC listed in steam, RaceRoom also has a store in game.
The price for cars and tracks beyond the given free ones are very reasonable compared to other sims that charge on a per car/track basis, this also enables the devs to keep adding new content consistently. Content is now available in packs for a discount as well. The neat thing is the way you get a scaling discount based upon how much of said pack you already own. Because I had already bought the DTM packs (DTM 2013 I picked up for a nice $7.50 on sale through steam dlc) and ADAC 2013 pack, when I went to buy the European track pack the remaining 3 or 4 tracks I didn't already own ended up costing me about 20% of what they would have if I bought them individually.
One really big thing for me being an Aussie is BATHURST!
It's probably the best most accurate version of the track ever made outside of laser scanning.
Yep, if you like racing cars with a wheel or even a gamepad, definitely make sure you check this one out.

As probably you already know this game requires a powerful PC. On my I7 with a decent graphics card I get around 20 fps, sometimes dropping to 10. I wouldn't say it's such a big problem for a train simulation game but one has to be aware of that before buying. While discussing performance let me mention that in general apart from pure FPS this game works better for me than original TS, which often freezes for a moment. It also had a bad feature that when frame rate drops the simulation time slows down. No such things in CSX.
Ok so now Let's discuss the game itself. In my opinion this is a big step forward into real immersion. While TS was just a train game with nice routes, CSX tries to be a real simulator. How? Let's see:
Almost every button is clickable. And most of them are not fake. If you want to start a cold loco you will have to do almost all the stuff you'd need to do in real life (ok maybe few steps were omitted). If you want to couple 2 or more locos to cooperate (to be driven from one cab) you will have to set up all of them properly. If you don't it won't work - either they won't listen or you won't be even able to release the brakes. There is no more switching locos or cabs by combination of buttons. You have to stand up and walk to another loco, enter it and sit down inside. Same with switching to another train. You will have to manually uncouple the cars. You can refuel your loco by plugging in the hose by yourself. You can operate the railway turntable, you can manually operate the switches. Etc. Believe me this really adds a lot to the immersion of working in the railways. As playing TS you just sit to run a scenario often tracing the HUD, here you can really try to simulate real operation.
Physics seems much better now than in original TS. For example if the brakes are not released on the train yet and you apply throttle forward, the train will stretch. If you now idle, you'd be pulled back like attached to a spring. This way by lack of gentle control you may induce a kind of oscillations in the whole train which could eventually lead to tearing it apart. Unfortunately I haven't checked that yet, but probably every coupler is physically modeled and it's stress calculated in real time.
Graphics is nice, maybe not breathtaking but still better than in original TS. Sounds are fine. HUD is better than in TS because it gives you all the important information (speed, air pressure etc., current limit) in one place while those things that might be read from the track (like speed limits, signals etc.) are shown on the track instead of the diagram. Still, I believe this game should be played hudless. The route isn't very hard to learn, there are not so many different speed limits and without the HUD, this game becomes a real simulator.
Speaking of the route. It's not that long maybe, but with average speed of about 30 mph it will take several hours to drive it through. Driving out of the yard itself might take like 15 minutes. So there is a lot of driving. Not that much actually happening on the route. Your main job will be to keep the speed under limit during climb by throttle and during descend by use of dynamic brake. Of course you should monitor signals and the track itself too. It's not one of those fast TS routes where you have to act all the time. It's much more relaxing experience.
What's the content inside? We have 9 basic learning scenarios 5 mins. each, 8 different standard scenarios ranging from 30 to 180 mins, covering both route driving and yard works. We also have a new mode in which we select a loco (there are 3 to chose from), weather and then we are presented with a timetable. We can choose a train from this timetable. For all three locos there are around 36 different trains to chose from. Each of them differs by time of departure and of course it's consist. I believe that this is a complete 24h timetable for the whole route so if we chose one train from the list we still can meet the other one on the route while driving. There is also an option where we start on foot in the yard and we can just get into any of the locos and do what we want.
Still I have a feeling this is and unfinished product. For example we are taught how to load coal into the cars or operate the turntable but there is no real reason for that as the timetables aim at driving the whole route, while scenarios are only few and only one really makes you load the coal and I think in one we use the turntable. Maybe it's just prepared for announced multiplayer which is not implemented yet. Still you will easily find few tenths of hours of gamplay now and if you want to drive every train out of the timetable, you'd need few hundred hours to do so.
Unfortunately as for a simulator the game still lacks some real rail things like for example: interaction with the dispatcher (radio, written permissions etc.). Some documentation like paper timetables, route descriptions (with speed limits etc.), some working schedules (for forming trains etc.). Real people switching the manual switches (now we can either get out of the train and do it personally or click on a switch in the route map while in real life we'd rather radioed someone to do it or we would had someone to switch them on board). Real procedures like checking the brakes with someone giving proper signals (apply, release and so on) etc. I really hope some of these things will be adressed. I know that original TS engine just lacked possibilities to implement these kinds of things but when you are making a new product why not?
To summarize - If you just want to play with a train for 30 mins. a day I'd rather buy another route for the TS. CSX is for hardcore gamers who want to learn a lot and are also capable of sustaining the boredom of train climbing a mountain with 25 mph speed. If you are ready for this kind of challenge and your CPU is strong enough, go for CSX. It's not more expensive than a single route for TS and gives a lot more of content.
Even more hardcore gamers migh feel a little dissapointed because while CSX ads a lot of realism to train driving it still lacks some important real life features and apart from some amateur productions, no commercial product even tries to adress all these things that are so common to the rails apart from only driving the train itself. CSX makes a step in the right direction but still it is only a step.

This is the start of what will be a fantastic new series for train fans. The level of detail the developers have achieved using the Unreal 4 engine and their Simugraph simulation engine is nothing short of amazing. The ability to walk on foot and move about the train and railroad just makes the game so much more immersive and really helps draw you in and allows you to appreciate the scale and detail of the trains and the route.
The trains, rolling stock and route are modelled in very fine detail. The lighting is also some of the best I've seen in a simulator.
The tutorials on offer help teach you the basics and there is a manual as well that details some of the more advanced functions such as setting up trains as multiple units. I would have liked to seen tutorials cover the trains in more detail such as performing cold starts but the information is at least available in the manual.
The game offers a selection of scenarios as well that cover some of the main areas on the route, the scenarios include some good voice-over work which is a nice touch.
There is also a service mode which is basically a 24-hour timetable of train services that run across the route that you can interact with as well, riding on or driving trains or just observing them on-foot.
The game does still need some optimisation work and given the level of detail its best played on a powerful computer. That said it is a brand new engine with some strong capabilities (64-bit, DX12 support) so the developers have alot of room to improve it.

Minecraft never got my attention any more than "oh, that looks neat". The idea of building a house and then what? Oooooo I have a house or a village or a Grand Castle! Good for you! Now what does it do? What do you do with it? That does not capture my intrest. You know what does? I can build a Grand Castle, pack it full of power generators, shields, engines and 'frikkin laser beams to go blow up anything I come across in the Galaxy.
Not all is fun and games in the 'verse though. There are issues. Glitches and bugs and bad coding, Oh My! Sometimes your turrets will teleport themselves halfway across the sector. Sometimes your ship wont fully load and it looks like you are missing half of it. Weapons 99% of the time work great, 1% of the time, they work about as good as a screen door on an airlock.
Yes, the Devs are very active. They do listen to the players. Updates rather often. Unfortunatly, the updates do kinda break the game sometimes. But, they get patched, things are a little wonky for a few days, then its back. All is good.
I couldnt tell you how many new people Ive seen pop in on a server and start screaming "sum 1 halp me! I haz the dumb n dnt knw what 2 do!!!!!" This game offers a good balance between exploration and combat, all in a very enjoyable 2D platformer. The  non-linearity makes it even easier to have the one or the other depending on what you prefer. The progression is made by gaining new abilities, much like the new items you get in every dungeon in The Legend of Zelda; this really makes exploration interesting. The charms system makes it available for people with poor 2D skills (like myself) to adapt their fighting options to the boss they are struggling with, while good 2D platformers will go through the story smoothly and find tougher fights and tricky parkour challenges out of the main quest.

Call of Duty is easily the best WWII game on Steam. The levels feel exciting, the music provides an excellent complement to the atmosphere; the level design and AI is great.  The levels are all set pieces unto themselves, featuring a nice variety of scenery and objectives: shoot down planes, take out tanks, and kill Nazis by the scores. But I can’t really do justice to the game. The greatest strength of Call of Duty is that the game play feels both immaculately paced. Each mission feels like a fleshed out conflict that changes over the course of your playthrough, and the soundtrack lends each mission an air of significance. For its time, Call of Duty had some truly impressive set pieces. Each of the three campaigns brings a unique perspective and its own dynamics to the game, as the Americans seem to favor running and gunning over the Russian campaign, which feels more like a war of attrition. The first mission for the Russian army is perhaps one of the most intense I’ve played so far. As the Russian Army suffers heavy losses you make it out onto the battlefield without so much as a gun at your disposal. You dart through gun fire, saved ironically by Nazi artillery, which exposes a building. After taking the building by force, an artillery strike is called in. The salvos leave the several Nazi tanks in shambles, as the few Russian troops left scurry across the remains of a square in Stalingrad, you feel like you've actually pushed back the Nazi invasion.

i didn't read any reviews or descriptions and i thought the zup! games would be nice, relaxing puzzle games.
they were cheap.
i bought the bundle.
i played the first one. i played the second one. i played the third, and the fourth, and the fifth, and now here i am.
i feel dirty.
when i started playing i noticed that i was getting an awful lot of achievements. like, a lot. tons, even. i kept playing. i finished the first one and didn't really question why i had 118 achievements after playing a game for half an hour. i didn't really question why i was even playing the game. i just played it.
four thousand seven hundred and forty achievements later and i start wondering what i've been doing with my life. why have i been clicking the little red boxes? when did i start clicking them, and when did i lose track of the fact that i was clicking them? when did they turn into circles? when did the blatant portal rip-offs appear?
i didn't know. i still don't know.
my mind started to wander and i started asking myself more questions. was zup! even a game? was the thing i was doing even considered playing a game? i didn't know, but i continued on.
i continued to unlock achievements. more and more and more of them. so many that there was a constant flow of notifications in the corner. steady and constant. i didn't know what i was doing to achieve them, but there i was. achieving them.
i found that the constant stream of achievements was mesmerizing. near the end i was paying more attention to watching them all pop than the actual game. one achievement, two achievements, three, four, five...
i don't know where along the journey that i realized i was playing an achievement simulator. probably fairly early. i didn't stop though. after all, i paid for these games. because they looked like relaxing puzzles. because they were cheap.
regardless of when i realized it, i kept clicking.
four thousand seven hundred and forty achievements.
four thousand seven hundred and forty achievements.
four thousand seven hundred and forty achievements.
where did they all come from?
time had become an abstract concept. how long had i been clicking? how long had the steady stream of achievements been going for? how long would it continue?
when i finished this one, the fifth one, i checked my achievement progress. i was missing some. i felt compelled to complete them all and so i started clicking randomly. eventually i was rewarded thirty achievements for clicking the settings button.
i stopped after that. i felt... unclean. dirty. i had a shower. and i still feel dirty.
i don't think the zup! will ever wash away. i will have to live with what i've done. and i will, because life goes on and i must continue living.
after all, i have to find out what's at the end of zup! zero.
more achievements, i can only assume. but i won't know until i try, and so i will carry on, live on, to see if i can escape what i can only assume is some level of zup! hell.
edit: i initially had this as recommended. i don't know why. probably still mesmerized by the achievement stream. i do not recommend anything about zup!

(written after the custom shapes update)
[Intro]
Firstly, before the content, many people may have seen outdated reviews and I would like to clear up some things. They have creative mode. They have slabs like in minecraft. They have teleporters. Missiles aren't the most powerful weapon in the game.
This is one of my favorite games, not just because of its current state, but the timeline looks amazing. There are some bugs that appear every once and a while, but the devs are the best and always listen to what the community is saying.
If none of the stuff below sounds appealing, remember that the demo is the same thing as the full version! You can even play on servers and stuff, however in the future they will limit the demo.
[Description (longer)]
You can do a lot in this game. It comes with lots of colors (teal and pink are somewhat new), weapons and details. And pirates to blow up.
To start off, the controls take some time to get used too, and you can change them if you must. A lot of people gave this negative reviews just because of the controls, so ignore them. I prefer the default controls.
In terms of building, it is the opposite of minecraft. (left click to build) They have all sorts of hull colors and decorations you can use to make your ships look realistic. With the new addition of slabs and "custom shapes" - which means models / 3D indented stuff - ships have gotten to look way cooler.
Real quick, I also want to mention that the textures at their current state tend to look a LOT better and more polished than in outdated videos. The lighting is amazing right now too.
In terms of weapons, they have a lot too. What's so special is that you can combine up to 3 weapons to make one weapon better. For example, cannons make things shoot a lot faster, but reduce the damage a little. Missile computers hooked up with beams make homing missiles. They even have modules specifically for modifying weapons like push and pull effects.
In terms of factions, the player created ones work pretty well, however the devs are still working on the AI. It may take a while, however I am excited to see how they turn out based off of their posts.
Crew really can't do anything right now, so don't expect the option to "hire crew" to do much. Like I said the developers have large plans and continue to update it every two weeks, so to me it sounds very promising.
[Similar games]
I have seen some similar games like this. First off, space engineers is aimed to be more of a survival and realistic game, FROM WHAT I HAVE SEEN. (it doesn't work on my laptop or my pc :p) So I wouldn't compare it. Blockade runner seems very similar too, however I don't know much about it. The pictures online tell be that starmade is a MUCH more polished game, however starmade has been in development a lot longer to my knowledge.
[Short Description (for people like me)]
A block-based building game where you can build the ultimate space ship that actually functions and blast pirates & things with it. This includes hangers for drones or friends and warp drives to get around. Stations are an option too; you can process ores from planets and keep your ships safe there. Multiplayer? Team up with friends for fun or fight to the death in a battle of empires.
[Conclusion]
So that is really all I have to say. Don't underestimate what this game is aimed to be; just look at the dev. plans. Don't base your opinion off of old reviews, especially ones that say it just crashes. (unless you have a bad computer. Read the reccomended system first) I hope you think this is good if you buy it. Schine is really serious about its quality and brings constant updates. (if 2 every weeks is constant for you)
[Last note]
I haven't actually played the custom shapes update yet; just came out like an hour ago. Also, try out the demo if you aren't quite sure yet.
