I've been playing this game for awhile before it hit steam so my hours might be a bit skewed.  I'm gonna list some features I like below, and as the game grows I will add onto this list, and other things.
-Liked Features ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-People don't move or skit around when on ships. This is a big one, and a lot of space building games have players glitching or even getting stuck in walls becuase they don't treat the ship as a anchor.

-Much like an open world game. If you see it you can probably go to it. This game blows my mind on how expansive it is. You see that red dot in the distance? Thats a star, you can go there. That yellow dot? Another star. Seriously this game is crazy with this stuff and it blows my mind.
-Populated servers. If you haven't played on a server yet do it. Great expierence.
-Movable Asteroids. Its just fun to push them around, or even use them for cover.
-Block Variety. This is another big one for me becuase its real nice to have a large list of blocks just to build nice looking ships with.
-Advanced & Basic building. You can go very advanced with building in this game to get the most efficiency out of ships, or you can go basic, and get a alright ship.
-Logic Systems. Probably one of the best things a building game can include, absolutely amazing!
-Planets. You can even orbit them, or mine them out! Seriously planets are amazing they even have there own axis of rotation.
-Wormholes. You can travel throughout the galaxy on wormholes.
-Pirates. While they variety is lacking in the base vanilla game, you can add in your own Custom Pirates into the game.
-PVP. Great expierence this one its fun watching two giant frigates battle it outside a planet.
-Weapon Combinations. Probably one of my favourite features. Being able to combine a Rocket with a Cannon to make a shotgun is just the best.
-Breaching. It was done alright fun as all hell though.

-Shipyards. Absolutely amazing. Although I don't use it much its really fun to see a friend dock his        ship into our base.
- Great Tutorial. Gotta say helped me out a bunch!
~Developers + Support Team~ --------------------------------------------------------------------
- While I am not a developer my self I will say that they probably have one of the best support teams and dev's I have seen in early acess. I reported a bug about a wormhole spawning in my spawn when I first got the game and within a day it was on the bug tracker and my issue fixed! The developers also keep frequent updates, and are amazingly active on the forums.

- The demo is the full game. This is amazing for early access you are giving players a chance to play the game, and see if they want to support you! Great move on the creators.
- If you are gonna do early acess this is how you do it right!
~Servers~ -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- My expierence with servers have been fun. If you are gonna play starmade you absolutely gotta do it in a server. The game normally feels empty in singleplayer but in multiplayer servers usually add there own custom pirates, and tons of players populate the game! Seriously give this a shot.
~Community~
- Probably one of the friendliest communities I have ever met! Seriously they are a major help and I suggest you visit the forums here. "
"

A review isn't a review without some bad things. The game is still early acess so I won't really put bug complaints here.
(This list may grow)

UPDATE6/17/15------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Well, the game keeps getting better, and better.  It certainly has taken some time to get here, but the game and its content very, very good.  The recent patch has made a number of much needed updates and optimizations.  The dedicated servers has seen the online community grow, Tracks like Shanghai and Macau and cars like WTCC 2014 have really set this sim apart.
I have no idea how this game has such a low comunity score....well I do, its the F2P model...which really isn't F2P....I would really give it a go, the cars and tracks are some of the best done of all the big sims out there, iRacing, Pcars, AC, imo.
UPDATE 11/01/14----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
So I bought a wheel G27, and am really enjoying the game.  Much better with a wheel, although a controller was decent and has some advantages, but it is really not the way to go with a sim.
The updates that have been done have massively improved the game:  Time of day, updated Force Feedback, track and car physics improved(check to see if which cars and tracks are updated).  It still has a way to go, but is so much better.
The WTCC cars are a blast.  The ADAC GT cars are big heavy beasts.  DTM is somewhere in the middle.  Once the game gets a championship(pit stops and tires) and MP gets out of Alpha there will be a very, very solid game here.
I would definitely check it out...it is starting to take up a chunk of my life!

I am new to "sim" racing games.  Always loved a good race game in my youth (a while ago now), Super Monaco GP, Daytona,  Ridge Racer etc...  I bought Ridge Racer Unbounded for a couple of bucks and forgot how much I enjoyed racing games.  The drifting was so absurd, but it was fun.  I started looking at other types of racing games and saw this one and it was Free to play.  UGHH.  No harm no foul trying a F2P game.  It doesn't cost anything.  I figured I would download the game, play it for a week and then be done with it…
Well fast forward a couple of weeks; I am having a great time.  Using an Xbox controller, this took a long time to calibrate correctly.  It was quite a challenge at first, I like difficult games.  I really want to upgrade to a wheel... but patience!  I don't really understand most people’s complaints with the game, it seems most people/reviews say the game would be really good if this or that was fixed.  A majority were very minor complaints but together resulted in poor reviews.  The core of the game is strong, but there are issues with the game.  I can forgive them at this point since it is still in Beta and I haven't spent a penny on it.  The game has potential to be a LOT of fun as areas are improved and features added, but it will be interesting to see if the studio can get this title to that point - With the restructuring of the studio, hopefully they continue to improve the game at an acceptable pace! :)

I like the gameplay, pretty fun so far despite the horrendous PC port. There's inconsistent texture quality throughout the game, I was expecting better from the screenshots. I also had to fix my graphics driver because the game uses my integrated graphics card by default.
More details:
1. The game is 30 fps locked, not a big issue for me. But I experienced frames at 10~20 fps and had to go to my graphics settings to make sure the game uses my NVIDIA card instead of Intel's integrated graphics.
2. Inconsistent quality of graphics/textures. Some parts of the game looks nice, while others still look like you're playing from the PSP. I was expecting more from an HD remaster on PC.
3. This port has only either 720p or 1080p resolution. My laptop has a 900p resolution so it doesn't look too appealing on full screen. I had to keep it on a window that occupies only 65% of my screen.
4. People seem to be having trouble playing it on a keyboard and mouse. Highly recommended to use a controller, preferably Xbox controller for Windows.
Unless you're playing on a 1080p screen and have a good controller, I don't fully recommend purchasing this game as it is right now. Maybe after they fix the resolution and textures or after I fully enjoy the game.

A genuinely good puzzler.  The controls are simple: A & D move you, left & right arrows spin the world, W triggers doors and inverters.  Some levels take careful planning, and even when you see how to solve the level, working out how to make it happen can be tricky as well!  6 rooms in each of 4 levels, and then the same mirrored; 48 levels in all.  I thought the mirrored levels would be simple, but while the room is a mirror of the original, there are other twists to add challenges to them as well.
The game's artwork is again, simple, but genuinely good.  The levels are black & white, but animated in a similar manner as old cartoons; things like the shading of the doors changing from frame to frame, giving it a mild flicker.  It's delightfully charming and a nice touch.
Overall, a highly recommended puzzler.

Starmade is ultimately a great but unfinished game, its lacking an easy guide to learn some of the harder concepts (except youtube videos but that medium has a host of issues on its own, its hard to pick out the useful stuff from them.)
With the addition of the rail system the creative side of the game has reached new heights, want to make a mech? Go for it. Be able to have your ship open up into a scary looking superweapon? Yep once again.
Main problems with the game.
-Starmade has a grind and it doesn't really tell you how you could have avoided most of it. For example in the current version? Shops are almost useless if you want to make big ships. Credits are  a pain to get and you get more resources if you look into "server.cfg" in your starmade folder, set the mining multiplier to x5 and just mine planets.
- Logic and rails, the two best features for ship design in my opinion, are both rather hard to get into. Even if you figure out the theory trying to make something like two doors, of which only one may be open (think airlock) can be a struggle for a newcomer.
-Default config needs work. Not getting around this, default mining multiplier is terrible. Default speed is too low too.
- One final thing I'd like is some sort of safe area of space in which pirates will obviously not spawn, again for the new guys in SP or serverside getting shot right out of the gate is just a pain.
This game also has a lot of pros, not just cons. But if I were to write all that I'd liked I would be here all day.

Do you love
If you answered every question with yes then this a game for you. Hollow Knight is a metroidvania game with a mix of Dark Souls thrown into the mix. You navigate through maze-like tunnels, catacombs and grottos all with your trusty needle as your weapon. The Dark Soul-esque part comes into play when you lose all your health. If that happens you lose all your hard earned cash which drops from enemies, hidden rocks or chests. If you can make it to the room where you died alive you can recover all of it. But don't fear the combat. Every hit on an enemy gives you soul which you can exchange to get health or later for executing special attacks. A little map that you can upgrade can show you the way. You will need it for the way back to the dreaded bosses which are beautifully designed and have all their own mechanic.
All in all Hollow Knight is a beautiful drawn Soul-esque action adventure and deserves a look.

Other than that, think of it as a sort of low-tech XCOM in terms of the combat. It's based on a system of action points for moving and shooting and overwatching and guarding. Generally a must have for any 40k fan as supporting 40k games can only encourage more of them, right? On the whole i'd give this game a 6.8. It's not unenjoyable, it's actually fairly enjoyable, but it's not a binge-play, you should only play one mission a day.

When I saw the trailer for this game, it was clear that this was everything I could want in a video game, but it wasn't clear to what extent this was everything I could want in a video game until I played it.
The game is full of welcome surprises. So if you hit just about any motorized vehicle with your sword, it will immediately blow up, and likely blow up everything around it. This also goes for vending machines and arcade games. If a game object doesn't blow up, it will likely be broken into many pieces when you hack at it with your sword. So, if you play video games like me, you will run around the whole game waving your sword around hacking at stuff until you blow up and have to restart from the last checkpoint.
In a related note, there are bunnies throughout the game, and when you hit them once with your sword they will explode with blood and guts. So, naturally, every time I see a bunny, I slice it up. Well, I whacked one bunny with a sword and, sure enough, the background music changed to heavy metal and it became a black demon bunny. It jumped around really quickly an I had to hit it dozens of times before it would ♥♥♥♥ing die. I'm just playing this game saying "what the ♥♥♥♥".
Also, the amount of humor related to the fact that your character is named "wang" is much more than I expected. At one point the character says "I guess they couldn't handle all that wang".
But on a really serious note, it seems like these days many of the games I buy just kick my computer's♥♥♥♥♥ But this game manages to have incredible graphic fidelity AND run on ultra on my computer with a noticeably high framerate. It's clear the developers actually put effort into making this game run efficiently, which I believe most mainstream developers do not care about at all (mostly because they are targetting consoles and once they get those versions to a certain framerate they just don't care, and obviously don't care enough to do a good PC port).

I enjoy playing challenging puzzle games alot as it's nice to have my brian be the deciding factor on whether I win or lose and not the skill at using mouse and keyboard. So I bought this interesting game for just 70p to see what it's like. I was rather disappointed.
The game delivers a nice looking world with each level that is fun to look at as the landscape is very confusing, using quirky optical illusions to distort the map. This I really liked but in the way of puzzle gameplay it was slow and not very challenging. I found I could complete most levels through just using trial and error once or twice to get to the end instead of actually using my brain to figure out where I was meant to go and how I was supposed to minipulate the terrain (yes this can be considered a fault on my part and I respect that). The one time I did use my brain to track my steps through the puzzle world was more like going through a maze than completing a puzzle, not a very puzzling level.
Another reason I don't recommend it is the progression through the levels is not at all rewarding. The story was not at all interesting if at all existent, and the reason I say this is because at the end of each level there was a thought for you to read. It did not tell a story or explained why this was happening, it was just nonsense. This coupled with the very uninteresting new components added each chapter, left me with no motivation to continue through the levels to discover what was at the end. It also didn't help that the character walks the pace of a snail, "If you would like to get there this life time that would be great."
What I did like about the game was the ability to warp back in time when you failed, instead of completely restarting the game. Having to restart every time I died, keys flying off the map, boulders getting too up close and personal, would of been very irritating. The map design was very clever with all the optical illusions and the confusing layout, with the added art form the maps where nice to look at and very unique.
The game is unique with map and puzzle design but not fun to play and gives no reason to continue playing.

Quite possibly the best AC game to date, rivaling even the beloved Assassin's Creed 2.  Black Flag takes all of the elements of past games that you love from the stealth and parkour to the battles and story improves them, then adds to them.  The combat system no longer feels like counter after counter and now flows with secondary items fitting into the mix very well.
The game also stays fresh by adding a fun, and exciting new element through sailing and ship battles.  Rather than becoming a tedious nuisence like one might expect, fighting on ships and upgrading one's vessel is fun and rewarding, allowing you to take on truly fearsome opponents and capture enemy ships for your own use.
Some long time fans of the series critize this game for not being a true Assassins game as for much of the game the protaganist is not truly an assassin.  In my opinion however the game does something far more interesting than tell the story or an assassin.  It tells the story of someone who becomes one.  You learn his motives and watch as he adopts the creed because he believes in it, not because he was born into it.  Something I find to be more compelling.
The only downside to this game are the parts that take place in modern day.  You play a voiceless protaganist working in Abstergo and hacking computers to learn more about the world.  All in all it's very boring and adds nothing to the game itself let alone the overarching plot.  Still it's owrth playing and is definitely a better buy than Unity or Rogue.

Developed by the geniousness of Davey Wreden, "The Stanley Parable" is an enjoyable, funny and interactive fiction video game, with a perspective resembling the first-person one.
You should not expect complicated controls, as the main character you play, being Stanley, can only move around and interact which certain objects.
But here comes the peculiar feature of this game: every single step you take, every single decision or action you make is commentated and presented by the the voiceover of the game's narrator.
It is up to you from the very beginning what to do, since thestory splits in different amounts of possibilities: will you choose to follow all the narrator's instructions? Will you disobey him? And what if you do both?
This will be your chance to try to shape your story, sometimes setting the voice angry, other times almost creating a deep relationship with him.
You are left alone, who can stop you from doing what you desire?

So I'm going to rewrite this review now that I've had most of my issues fixed, the game is consistently playable, and change this to a recommended review. Of course, there is a big asterisk to that, because the game can be laggy to the point of unplayable if you don't have the correct graphics settings. (There is luckily a steam guide to explain that as well as a
of the graphics options.) Also, with the Sept 18th patch, full-screen mode is fixed as well as having an expanded resolution compatibility.
The key point I'd like you to keep in mind is don't play this game with the keyboard. It's just weird. (Apparently, the Sept 18th patch also added some mouse changes, but yeah, play with a controller. For some weird reason, on the keyboard my camera controls will not work on one of my computers.) The game plays beautifully with a controller (my preference are the PS3/PS4 controllers, but the game is set to Xbox as a default).
The game itself is of the standard Final Fantasy variety with an epic score and indepth story, but with an action RPG twist. Expect long cutscenes like the other games of the series for one. (I did notice this FF is particularly bloodier than the others and it feels darker with the characters plunged into war.) Unlike other FF games, you have a wopping selection of 14 playable characters so you can create your teams of 3 in a way you'd like (except for the first mission/prologue where your team is set for you). The team AI isn't brilliant, but they're mainly there for you to change characters as you need (short range versus long range, for example). It plays similar to a Kingdom Hearts game where you have to dodge as needed, and your HP will refill if you stand still.
The game is set in the form of missions, but there is a 'downtime' between each where you can wander the academy and stock up on items/weapons, view history/lore or previous cutscenes, or engage with NPCs to acquire items or see more story tidbits. While you can technically wander without a timer, certain actions will drop your remaining time until the next mission. Once it's mission day, you can head out into an overworld which brings me back to classic FF games where you can either wander or head straight to the objective.
A lot of the complaints focus on the graphics since this is supposed to be HD, but remember this is a PSP port. The major characters are all updated while some of the minor characters and backgrounds are not. Some of the lipsynching seems a bit off (I do play in the original Japanese), but it's not a big deal for me.
The game originally had some major issues regarding playability upon release, and it may take some fiddling around to find out what settings work best for you, but once you figure it out, the game plays smoothly. Again, I wouldn't play this game without a controller, since there's still no keybind option. It feels like a bloodier, but with the story and characters of a classic, FF game, and I can finally recommend it.

While I have always been moderately good at platformers, I am truly terrible at 2d fighting games.  So it is safe to say that I am horrible at this game.
Nonetheless, I find it to be one the most entertaining games in my library and one I see myself eventually 100% clearing.  I imagine it will take me 60-80 hours to do so (other people report around 30 hours to 100%) and I am looking forward to it.
For all you 30+ gamers out there whos' reflexes and attention spans just aren't what they used to be, I highly recommend this game.  It's easy to play 30 minutes or a couple hours at a time and has enough to explore to keep you wanting to go back.  The majority of bosses are optional, so your game doesn't come to a screaming halt because of a frustrating boss fight.  Instead you can go try out the bosses when you feel up to it (and just spent all your money so you have nothing to lose anyways).
The art style is excellent.  All hand drawn.  Mildly dark with a hint of cuteness.
Music is superb.  Haunting and inviting.  Reminiscent of 80's fantasy such as Legend, The Dark Crystal, The Last Unicorn.
Story is fine given that it's less of a story and more of an atmosphere being presented over the course of the game.
Gameplay is good.  Doesn't require insane twich dexterity to get through.  Can be frustrating when you die with tons of cash on you in a hard to get to place.  Spend your money while you have it! Controls seem a little sticky at times but that could just be my crappy old controller.
Overall 9/10     If they had put a little more effort into the story it would probably be a 10.

The Bridge is a fantastic little puzzle game filled with Escherian beauty. Unfortunately, it will often test not only your problem solving skills, but also your patience, especially if you're one of those relentless achievement collectors who accept nothing shy of game perfection. At times, you will feel like you're trapped on the steps of a Penrose staircase or endlessly sliding on a Möbius strip, but suddenly, in a glimpse of brilliance, you'll find the way out of the seemingly impossible, and you'll proudly embrace the next challenge while patting yourself on the head in an attempt to high-five your awesome brain. Sadly, to get a 20/20 score you'll need to rely on a bit more than just logic and creativity, and I think you shouldn't have to resort to pure chance, or a guide, to help you finish a puzzle game, but overall it's completely worth your time and money!

Stronghold Crusader 2 offers very little change from the previous Crusader (2001). Hardcore fans and achievement hunters will be the only ones who will appreciate SC2. The "Campaign" trails are back from the original. They offer no more than a series of AI skirmish challenges that vary in difficulty. There's a dozen or so tutorial missions the have some kind of "Narrative" but I use that word loosely.
Melee Fighting: Winning consists of massing a blob of units into another player's castle to kill thier avatar "Lord." I say "blob" because the units clip into each other It's not pleasing on the eyes when a group of a hundred pikemen can't be distinguished between a single guy. To make matters worse, during a fight they all clip into smaller blob. To make matters EVEN worse, a well placed pitch pot can decimate a group of hundreds.
Castle Smashing: The castle walls are no more than ten feet high and seem as strong as paper mache't. A few catapults can blast through a wall very quickly.  Probably why they removed ladder men and seige towers from the previous games. They added "ragdoll" physics, when a unit is arrowed they will tumble off the wall, if their foot doesn't get stuck and trap them hanging like maniquins for a few seconds before they disappear. When a tower falls with units on top the ragdoll levitates like Wil-e- Coyote holding up a sign before they fall to the ground.
Themes: The music is the only thing done right. Really great Crusade feeling soundtrack. As for the two religions, a lot of care was taken to avoid controversy. The Islamic Saracens dont eat the "pig" food ration (they grow sheep farms instead) and don't drink Ale, another handicap seeing as how they can't gain the happines benifits from Bars, and no other feature was put in place instead. Churches and Mosques are only distuinguishable from a little moon and star above the Mosque.
TL:DR= Only for fans of Stronghold. a lot of features done poorly, none really dont right. It's old Stronghold with new spit polish. Nab it on a sale and knock out the generous achievements.

Long story short: This game is worth well more than 15 bucks.
Before I get into the details, however, about me:
I am not a hardcore gamer, I don't play many games, and am fairly picky about what games I buy.
Hollow Knight is my first venture into this genre, so I cannot compare it to similar games.
I've played 33 hours at this point, and I think I'm far enough to judge this game.
Now...
Hollow Knight is an atmospheric puzzle-platformer with an emphasis on exploration and combat. When you start out you're dropped into a world with nothing but an old, cracked refashioned nail for a weapon. As you go along you gain ailities slowly. You often have to complete a challenging bit of aerobatics or defeat a boss or miniboss to gain a new upgrade, ability, or shop.
Upgrades themselves are fair, and never add too much in one go. Rather, they accumulate to make you more and more powerful.
The sounds and music in this game are crisp and beautiful. They really add to the atmosphere, and feel very real.
The artwork in this game is outstanding. Often utilizing dark colors, the hand-drawn world forms a solid foundation for the feel this game is going for.
Hollow Knight's controls are extremely responsive and thight, and the gameplay is fluid, with a fairly minimalistic hud, that doesn't display any real distractions. You feel like you are in complete command of your nimble character.
Combat is fast paced, and tight, and opponents get progressively harder as you go along.
Hollow Knight as exploration nailed. In part due to the massive world size, you feel as if it could go on forever. The anticipation of what's through the next tunnel is fascinating.
So, in conclusion, and once again, this game is completely worht 15 bucks.

Shadow Warrior is a truly good solid game. Worth every cent.
The game is set in a world invaded by demons, you play as the comedic Lo Wang, a sword slashing assassin. You get a funny demon pal in the first level named Hoji and he gives you kickass demon slaying powers to use throughout the game.
The Campaign- The story is really well done. I was interested the whole time and never really got bored. It was funny and there is a bunch of funny one liners and collectible fortune cookies that will keep you laughing. The story can be confusing at parts but by the end you will fully understand. Lo Wang and Hoji's conversations occur nearly at the end of every fight and in between. There aren't huge awkward pauses in dialogue. The game felt like a movie and had some feels moments and some action kickass moments.
The Gameplay - The game plays like a true arcade game, which it was. There's enough guns to keep you satisfied and there is a ton of different ways to slay your enemies. The base Katana which you get is obviously the best choice. You get kickass abilites for it and you get to slice off almost every limb on your enemies.
Gunplay is pretty basic , nothing to complain about but nothing too special either. Your abilities do not affect how your weapons work either which is hella convienient You can heal or force push or dash and you will still reload without interruption and keep fighting. The game is definitely linear and it can get a little bit repetitive at certain points. You search for money and ammo in the same containers, upgrade abilities and stuff throughout the game. It's fairly simple.
Enemies - The enemies deserve there own part. There is a large variety of enemies in Shadow Warrior and as the game progresses , the game will start giving less ♥♥♥♥s about how difficult it is (especially when it comes to the shamans. Seriously. ♥♥♥♥ those guys.). The game introduces new enemies alone then starts playing with different combinations leading up to a final fight before the boss fight that throws EVERYTHING at you. I'm giving you a fair warning. Learn how to combat each enemy type and get ready for that final volley because it's challenging. The game will test you beforehand by throwing random combos of enemies too. Use your environment to help you. You're not invincible either so make sure to keep up the heals.
Survival - It's pretty decent and self explanatory, not much to say there. More enemies and combos as you progress.
Summary/ TL;DR - Shadow Warrior is a solid action game with tons of different ways to fight, a solid campaign, a decent survival mode for replayability, and kickass gameplay. 10/10. Worth full price, but sale is always good too :)

Developed by the geniousness of Davey Wreden, "The Stanley Parable" is an enjoyable, funny and interactive fiction video game, with a perspective resembling the first-person one.
You should not expect complicated controls, as the main character you play, being Stanley, can only move around and interact which certain objects.
But here comes the peculiar feature of this game: every single step you take, every single decision or action you make is commentated and presented by the the voiceover of the game's narrator.
It is up to you from the very beginning what to do, since thestory splits in different amounts of possibilities: will you choose to follow all the narrator's instructions? Will you disobey him? And what if you do both?
This will be your chance to try to shape your story, sometimes setting the voice angry, other times almost creating a deep relationship with him.
You are left alone, who can stop you from doing what you desire?

Okay, I'm no expert on FF games because I don't have a console to play them on. So when they announced the Type-0 HD is coming to PC, I was honestly excited. Then something struck me, seeing the past ports from Square Enix, I had this looming fear of Type-0 HD being a bad port again.
Come release day, I got onto the discussion board in Steam and found an enormous amount of complaints about the game, not at all unexpected. From things that I feel are trivial to things that had some good claims to it. One of the most common problem I saw, was that the game runs very very badly with keyboard controls. So I decided to get a new controller, which I did. I went back home and started playing.
Here's the few problems I encountered and general problems that other players complain about.
1. The .exe straight crashes the moment I press "Start Game". (Solved it by setting Steam to run in Administrator mode)
2. Some pretty obvious texture differences. (But this issue doesn't really bug me too much since I've played Xenoblade Chronicles with the HD Retexture earlier, which causes the early stages of the game to look really good, but everything reverts to the original texture quality because the mod was unfinished. Anyway, I didn't expect it to look super awesome, which apparently many people who bought it was expecting, for some reason.)
3. The game locks at 30fps. (Which is to say, reaaaally not a problem for me at all, as long as it runs at constant 30, which it does. I never really understood the necessity for 60fps. FYI, I can see the difference, just not something worth fussing about for me. If the game's good, I don't care.)
4. Keyboard controls and the inability to rebind keys. (That was the reason why I bought a new controller in the first place. I would however, agree that this issue is probably the most noteworthy to complain about considering it's supposedly a PC game.)
In my 3 hours + experience with the game, I can honestly say that I like it, for now. The combat takes some getting used to but I really like the combat. I kept experimenting with different characters to see which one I like more than the other, and honestly I still don't have 3 favorite characters yet. I have little to no problems except for the hiccup during the first start of the game and that to me, is good enough. I'm really looking forward to continuing the game tonight after my work, honestly. I WANT to be invested.

Don't go into this expecting some polished PC port. It's a port of a port of a psp game.
With that out of the way, I've seen using an xbox controller and been having a blast. Plays better than the PSP original I played a while back, and so far there have been no crashes or major bugs. People seem to be complaining about camera and bad texture issues, but again, this is an updated PSP game. As long as you don't go into this thinking it's some AAA title, you'll enjoy it.
Combat is an interesting ARPG system, with an emphasis on dodge and timing your attacks. Button mashing attack can get you through battles, but it's faster and more exciting to use breaksight/killsight, which effective is a time window after/before certain enemy animations that give a huge bonus to damage. There's 14 playable characters, which all have unique enough styles and weapons that no two feel similar. For example, two ranged characters, King and Tres use a gun and bow respectively, but King requires a reload every 12 shots (upgradable) but focuses on high damage output. HoweverTres relies on precise timing, where charging your attack and waiting for breaksight/killsight is far more effect than spamming attacks.
I like the politically focused story, with an emphasis on the effect of war on people. Also to note, there's these breaks between missions which reminds you of the Persona series, in that you have various events, people to talk to that affect things later down in the game. Graphics are very good for an updated PSP game, but ultimately are inconsitent. There's relatively detailed character models but shoddy PSP textures behind them.
All in all, I'd rec this. It's a nice entry in the FF series that has key elements (airships, open world) but stands very uniquely in the FF series

Having played just about everything that 3D Realms produced in the nineties, I was very interested in this Shadow Warrior reboot.
It is true to the original, with updated graphics and gameplay elements. Lo Wang looks and sounds different, but the cheesy one liners, the ambiguous chinese/japanese setting and the humour are all there. Even the killer rabbits.
The levels are big, highly explorable like the original and other games from the early shooters, I must say I was surprised when I thought I had fully explored a map and found I had only gotten maybe 70% of the secrets found by the end.
The biggest gameplay improvement has to be the functionality of the sword, I find myself using it over any of the guns whenever possible, when it was pretty much a last resort weapon in the original (for me anyway)
There are also a upgrade/perk points/skill tree system which has some useful things like upgrades to weapons, more stamina/health etc. It's not too complicated and I found that improving all the sword related abilities made the game even more enjoyable.

The 30fps lock is annoying, and this game isn't graphically that great -- But then again this is a PSP game that never had the intention of ever being released on PC, or let alone in North America to begin with.  Plus it's sold at half the cost of retail on consoles.
It's a good game that will put Final Fantasy fans right at home with good story.  This isn't a main series entry, so go into it with the right mindset and it's a good experience.

I can't say enough good things about this game. Let's take a look at it piece by piece.
The main character is Lo Wang. He's a wisecracking super-hero fan that views himself as a badass. Although that seems somewhat cliched, he IS a badass and can hold his own from the very first fight. His one-liners get better as his personality evolves which is also pretty badass. He's a hitman working for Zilla who is essentially the most evil, most powerful, deadliest man on the planet. Zilla makes an agreement with some demons that starts the demon apocalypse, though both sides intend to double cross each other. Lo Wang meets and becomes partners with a demon named Hoji. Hoji has been banished from the Shadow Realm for unknown reasons. Lo Wang and Hoji journey across Asia assembling pieces of the only sword that can harm the demon leaders. On their journey they discover more about who Hoji is, and the story becomes more about Wang and Hoji each trying to redeem themselves in their own ways and distance themselves from the somewhat nefarious villains they each started as. You can genuinely see their attitudes and morals evolve over the course of the game and it's awesome.
The game at first seems like a hack n' slash with guns swapped in, but is actually really deep and diverse in gameplay. By the end of the game there are six guns in your belt along with your katana, and you can also use demon body parts against them if you upgrade your skills properly. On top of that there are seven super powers at your disposal. Weapons, skills, and super powers all use different systems with a variety of different upgrades trees. There's a huge variety of enemy types which keep you mixing all your abilities frequently to tackle them all. Nothing is overpowered because everything has a factor that keeps it from fighting uncontrollably. The game is mostly linear, though the side paths are there for those that want to explore and find collectibles, which are key to the uprade system. This game is a blast through and through.

Where to start....
For one, you only get 5 out of the 38 cars for free. The rest, you have to buy. Now, maybe this wouldn't be nearly as bad if you could actually choose the cars, but no. You're stuck with what they've already chosen, which means you could end up driving in a class of cars that you might not want two.
Secondly, ona similiar topic, you get 2 generic free tracks out of 14.
Third.I couldn't find a way to rebind keyboard controls. The handling system felt off as such. (I know this is supposed to be played with a wheel and pedals, but I've played plenty of sims without. rFactor 1 and 2, other SimBin titles, Assetto Corsa, etc.) The UI was pretty bad as well.

I'll jump right into describing some features.
Starmade's weapon system is one of its best features. You can achieve a great many different styles of weapons by combining them. There are four "slots" so to speak in each weapons system: a primary, a secondary, and effect, and a color. For example: a cannon primary, with a missile secondary will create a shotgun-like weapon. A missile primary with a pulse secondary will create a lethal, but slow, homing torpedo. A beam weapon with a cannon secondary will fire shorter bursts more rapidly. You can add an effect, like EMP which drains power from the target or pierce which adds a railgun-like effect. Each of these customizations can be applied at different strengths by altering the ratio of each system's size; i.e. a cannon with half as many missile blocks supporting it will only split into half as many shots. And finally by linking a light-emitting block, the shots from that weapon will turn that color! This allows extreme weapon customization that no other game of this type can even REMOTELY approach.
You can also create AI controlled automatic turrets using this same weapon system!
With all these weapons, it's a good thing that the game has a number of defenses besides plain armor. There's a working cloak and radar jammer, energy shields, and defensive effects used by activating the aforementioned "effect" systems by themselves. For example ion will temporarily divert extra power to your shields, and overdrive will increase your ship's maximum speed.
Starmade occurs on a galactic scale, including individual solar systems with planets that revolve around their suns, black holes that can serve as wormholes, jump drives and a detailed map available to the player. In multiplayer, factions can claim(and try to take) these systems, with the amount of territory they can hold dependent on their size and success. Paired with the much more detailed combat mechanics, this means that online multiplayer has the potential to be pretty epic.
As you can see, in some ways the game is incredibly fleshed out. But it IS early access- it is not complete. People looking for lots of realism will be also be disappointed(look at Space Engineers instead!)

If you want a long, fullfilling challenge I'll warn you: The Bridge is a relatively short puzzle game, unless you get stuck in a single place for long you should really be able to finish EVERYTHING in about five hours (Though you should find yourself a guide if you want the collector achievement, some are impossible to get without hints that, no, you won't find in game).
About the game in itself: the graphics are quite nice and lovely, if you love Escher you'll LOVE the game just by staring at its impossible graphics which, at the same time, make for mind-boggling puzzles.
Sadly, the mechanics of the game are NOT as complex as the graphics suggests...
As most puzzles games, expecially those where you control the world as well as your character, your abilities are limited (This time more by speed than actual limiting, but if a death-ball is between you and where you want to go forget about changing the world fast enough that you "skip" the ball: it'll follow you to your death)
This however makes the solution maybe too linear, sometimes making the user start to meta-think the solution (going left not because it'll lead me to the solution but because going right will kill me so it's obviously not the answer).
Adding more mechanics doesn't fix it, as essentially starts becoming "Okay, can't go left, nor right, I'll use that switcher there then."
The hardest levels try to fix this by relying more on momentum and timed movements, while they succeed I personally dislike those due to feeling "un-puzzle-like" to me.
The puzzles tend to be still challenging if you try to "understand" the solution, expecially due to the peculiar graphics making it hard to get a clear idea of what's going on the screen, so I suggest everyone playing this game to do this, but it lost some points due to being too weak to the "trial-and-error" solution.

A fantastic game with that wastes just a little too much time.
First off - buy the game, its 15 bucks, its great. Jumping feels good, progression feels good, sitting on a bench feels good. All while looking GREAT!
It is really good and you will enjoy it.
But I do have one gripe. I will use Dark Souls as a base for reference since (like most games nowadays) this game does as well. In Dark Souls, there would be a checkpoint, a bit of a run, and then a boss. So if the boss killed you you had to do that run a few times until you finally got your act together and killed the boss. This does exactly that, but the run is much more dull because its just a bunch of jumps with very few enemies and no real point... If Dark Souls didn't exist I would be baffled by the reasoning to put the checkpoints so far from some of the bosses because it just doesn't work on the same level as its inspiration.
As I was playing I was wondering why this irritated me so much, and I realized its because this game also pulls heavily from metroidvania types, where you are constantly finding things that you can't quite interact with becuase you need a power up... which is also something that just basically wastes your time. I sorta wish this element was a bit more like Dark Souls where exploration always seemed encouraged, and the only reason you would turn away from an area was because a dude seemed too tough for you instead of being like... yea i wish I could freaken ground pound, guess I'll try to remeber this spot to slog back to later.
Both of these things stacked together make some play sessions feel incredibly wasteful, and while its the inherent to the type of game it is, it just slightly tips the scale on this one.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

I just submitted a request for a refund -- I would not suggest picking this one up, which is a shame because I would love a good JRPG right about now.
Some issues --
1) I have not had issues with FPS dips that others have had, and I don't mind the general graphic quality of the game -- what drove me crazy was how inconsistent the game was visually.  Some character models appear to have been updated for the "HD" release, but others were not.  Some textures look good, some look awful.  Some effects appear to have been upgraded (there's some real-time rendered fire in the intro section that is brilliant), and some is god awful.   The constant disparity in quality makes the lower-end sections / characters / textures / effects really stand out, in a bad way.
2) Too many circa 1999 PC gaming design issues.  Having to exit the game to a launcher to change certain settings (or fix issues, like the on-screen prompts changing from controller input to keyboard for whatever reason) should not be a thing in 2015 game from a "AAA" publisher.
3) The controls are just not good.  Keyboard isn't even an option -- unless you like the idea of controlling the camera with the numpad.  I find the controller support baffling -- you can already switch targets with the left and right triggers, but they made it so you can also switch targets by nudging the right stick.  Why is this an issue?  Early in the game, I was on a bridge with ranged targets attacking me from up high on buildings / ledges up and across gaps.  I switched to a ranged character and tried to turn the camera to survey how many enemies there were.  Unfortunately, the camera was zoomed in to the point I could hardly see anything.  Every time I tried to move the camera, the game interpreted it as a target lock change.  The result?  The camera was just spinning circles around my character, and with the god-awful motion blur I couldn't see a damned thing.
4) The early combat was very button-mashy.  I couldn't tolerate the game long enough to see if this changes.
5) The game is tonally strange.  The game opens up with more blood and combat-honesty than I can recall having ever seen in an FF game -- and brings in your RAH RAH GOOOOOO HIGH SCHOOL SUPER POWER SQUAD heroes.  The gravitas from the opening is quickly lost.
6) The voice acting was not terrible, but the voice SYNC was horrid.  Spoken lines were frequently off from lip flaps by at least 0.5 seconds.  Bat voice-to-animation syncing drives me crazy, don't know why.  This may not be an issue for others, but it's bothersome for me.
I really, really wanted to like this game -- I had some hope after getting a chance to play the Episode Duscae demo for FF XV on PS4, and was readily impressed.  I've been in the mood for a good JRPG, but this was definitely not it.  Hopefully Tales of Zesteria will fill that void.

I can't say enough good things about this game. Let's take a look at it piece by piece.
The main character is Lo Wang. He's a wisecracking super-hero fan that views himself as a badass. Although that seems somewhat cliched, he IS a badass and can hold his own from the very first fight. His one-liners get better as his personality evolves which is also pretty badass. He's a hitman working for Zilla who is essentially the most evil, most powerful, deadliest man on the planet. Zilla makes an agreement with some demons that starts the demon apocalypse, though both sides intend to double cross each other. Lo Wang meets and becomes partners with a demon named Hoji. Hoji has been banished from the Shadow Realm for unknown reasons. Lo Wang and Hoji journey across Asia assembling pieces of the only sword that can harm the demon leaders. On their journey they discover more about who Hoji is, and the story becomes more about Wang and Hoji each trying to redeem themselves in their own ways and distance themselves from the somewhat nefarious villains they each started as. You can genuinely see their attitudes and morals evolve over the course of the game and it's awesome.
The game at first seems like a hack n' slash with guns swapped in, but is actually really deep and diverse in gameplay. By the end of the game there are six guns in your belt along with your katana, and you can also use demon body parts against them if you upgrade your skills properly. On top of that there are seven super powers at your disposal. Weapons, skills, and super powers all use different systems with a variety of different upgrades trees. There's a huge variety of enemy types which keep you mixing all your abilities frequently to tackle them all. Nothing is overpowered because everything has a factor that keeps it from fighting uncontrollably. The game is mostly linear, though the side paths are there for those that want to explore and find collectibles, which are key to the uprade system. This game is a blast through and through.

Dungeon Defenders is a pretty amazing tower defense game that has many layers and a deep well of potential strategies and tactics.
Don't let the cartoon graphics fool you, as this game is quite hardcore at heart.   When you get to a certain point you will be grinding for gear like you couldn't imagine.  If you are a fan of grinds (as I am in many situations) it should be a good fit for you.
Even if you don't enjoy a grind-style endgame, you can still get many hours of enjoyment out of Dungeon Defenders, though.  There are plenty of maps and characters to master, and if you don't feel the need to increase the difficulty level beyond what you're comfortable with, you won't be forced to.
If you can pick it up in a pack with all the DLC it is even better, as there are some genuinely interesting DLC classes and game modes.

The Bridge is an interesting game with its flaws.
The gameplay is a bit dull, which mostly consists of getting to the other door with the use of keys. Besides basic movement, you can tilt the levels clockwise or anticlockwise, and are also able to reverse time. Unlike Braid however, reversing time isn't used for puzzles, only to reverse a game over. The tilting can also get annoying at times, feeling more like a precision game then a puzzle game at time.
Nevertheless, the game does try to spice the gameplay up by adding new rules as you progress (which isn't too much, only 4 worlds and 4 mirrored but a lot harder worlds) and with a very compelling artstyle. The Bridge is by no means an incompetent game. It's a puzzler, with a quirky but pleasing art style, plenty of content, and an appropriately large level of difficulty. I might even have recommended it a few years ago. But I've since been spoiled by puzzlers of tremendous quality, like Braid, Fez, Portal, and (more controversially) The Misadventures of P.B. Winterbottom.
In each of the above, the puzzles are soluble only with some kind of bright spark of an idea, with a relatively simple execution. In The Bridge, the puzzles often come down to trial and error, until eventually you arrive at a relatively complex execution. So, instead of a cathartic flash of inspiration at the end of a puzzle, instead you get a mild feeling of relief as the gauntlet is over.
Perhaps if The Bridge had a more engaging style, like the above puzzlers do, its more grinding puzzles would not hold it back so. As it stands, The Bridge shoots for atmospheric, which it achieves to a limited extent. However, the atmosphere is too thin and too monotonous to really persuade me to come back to it. In the end, very little motivates me to actually play the game.
If it's on sale, you might as well pick it up. Like I said, it's not an incompetent game. But, it's not worth full price, in my opinion.

Perhaps since Nintendo and Konami have been lax in maintaining the two series from which the genre take its name Metroidvanias have become overly represented in the indie scene. Hollow Knight manages to rise above the pack as one of the best exploration focused platformers to not feature Samus, Alucard, or a Belmont.
Beneath the unassuming town of Dirtmouth lies the cavernous Hollownest, a giant system of caves that hold the ruins of a one great civilization. You descend into the depths to face what creatures remain and find cryptic answers about what happened and how your character ties into it. Hollow Knight feels a little linear at first, but after the first few areas the world opens up more and you're free to explore in a bunch of different directions, and while the game does a good job of pointing you in a certain direction you have a bunch of different routes available to you as well as shortcuts to and from areas if you're able to suss them out.
Along the way you'll fight dozens of different enemies, fight a lot of challenging bosses (this is not a game for someone who's not willing to die a bunch to figure out how a boss works), and stumble into a lot of varied environments. One of my favorite parts of the game was just seeing the visual theme for each new area. Some are quiet and tranquil, some are dark and foreboding, some are lush and full of life, and others are dessicated and lifeless.
Mechanically the game is solid and the platforming and combat allow for you to manuever your way around some really tricky platforming and boss patterns. I like the lack of healing items in lieu of a soul (magic) meter that refills when you attack enemies. Healing takes a moment to charge so there's always a risk and challenge in finding just the right moment to get a tick or two of health in and since you need to fight to refill your magic you can't remain passive and play it safe. The importance of using your magic for healing meant I rarely used the game's attack spells since standard physical combat is so effective. There are equppable charms to offset this, but then again why not just equip charms to make your physical attacks even better?
I also thought the game could have used more movement abilites. I know alot of the harder platforming challenges are designed around the game's relatively basic set of platforming skills and more abilities might break them, but as I got further in the game I found that
required a lot of backtracking. Moreso than I recall ever having to go through in any Metroids or Castlevanias I've played. While the game was packed with enough secrets that I was still finding new items, rooms, and hidden boss fights I'd missed up until the end it does get tedious to return to old areas several times without new ways to traverse them and I felt like I experienced that with most areas in Hollow Knight at some point.
That being said I loved the bulk of Hollow Knight enough for that to be a minor quibble and I reccomend it to anyone with an interest in Metroidvanias.

I wanted to like this game a lot. I am a huge fan of both Metroid and Dark Souls, and I thought that this game was the perfect combination of the two. It looks so promising while looking at their trailers and when others play the first few levels, and that's because those parts of the game are actually good. But the game quickly becomes stale, spammy, full of RNG and, for lack of a better term, BS.
Let me start off by explaining the
things about this game.
1. The art style is quite impressive. I truly like the way this game looks. However, there are some things that I wish that they had done differently. More on that later.
2. The soundtrack fits the style of the game quite well. Bleak, barren, quiet, peaceful.
3. In terms of $/hour, this game is a steal. A 100% playthrough will definitely take you about 30/40 hours.
4. The first few hours of the game are incredible. You can see the polish that they put into the game at this point. The levels are well designed with lots of little secrets, and challenging bosses. You want to go explore to find new moves to make you stronger and faster.
But it quickly degrades once you reach the ~20 hour mark in your playthrough.
All the areas begin to look similar and don't really give you that same feeling that the first few did. Some of the areas look like they were made by a monkey with a two day deadline who can cut and paste (cough cough White Palace).
The music clearly shows signs of lackluster. Bleaker than bleak. Just a few piano notes here and there, if not just howling wind. I understand that that kind of music definitely fits some areas of the game, but there definitely could have been more added to the music than just some wind and some random piano notes.
The amount of backtracking required just to reach certain areas again is ridiculous. I want to be able to quickly get from place to place, not spend 10 minutes dashing through enemies and checking my map to make sure that I took the correct corridor. This could easily be fixed by adding even one more Stag Station for fast travel near
, because most areas you can get to quite quickly.
And then my major gripe with the game comes along: the combat is no longer fun at this point, and the skill required to beat certain bosses becomes "how well can you dodge homing projectiles?" as opposed to "how well can you predict this enemy's movement, have good spacing, know when to attack and heal, etc." Major offenders include
.
To add to that problem, the hit/hurtboxes are absolutely abysmal. The reasoning behind this, I'd imagine, has to do with the art style. The game would suck if you got hurt by jumping over something with large horns, so let's just make it so that the hitbox is smaller. But then you think "where is the sweet spot for me to not get hit on this enemy?" So you will consistely be spending time getting hit by enemies that you aren't clipping into at all, or not being hit by enemies that you are clearly inside of. I'm not sure what would be the best way to fix this, because if they just made the hitboxes based on your character overlapping with an enemy, it'd be even worse.
If you don't intend on beating this game, and only play the first 75% of it, then by all means get this game. But only pay 75% of the price, because 25% of this game is severely lacking polish, and will just make you question every choice the developers made.

This game seems to be getting a lot of negative reviews, most of which I disagree *cough* less than 10 hours logged *cough* but more to the point. Final Fantasy Type-0 is a port over from a PSP platform therefore I was not expecting what is actually received from the game in terms of the fighting system so cudos on that. Still like all games there is always pros and cons.
The "CONS" list is short so I will start with that.
1.If there is one thing I hope they patch it is this: There is a fundamental part of the combat system where you have to collect phantoma from bodies by locking your camera onto them. Not only does it take time for the character to start collecting but once the phantoma is collected the body evaporates but the camera is still locked onto the spot where the body was and either takes a while to budge or will not let you switch targets unless the enemy is in your range of sight or you toggle the "lock-on" comand off. This disrupts the flow of combat entirely and in closed spaces has gotten me killed more than I can count. You can get over it either by killing everything quick and hoping you did it fast enough that the bodies are still there or picking and choosing what to kill and harvest first.
2.With the combat system having you switching target to target in rapid succession I do not see this game being very enjoyable to play with a mouse and keyboard especially with the "lock-on" being funky. My advice is to break out a ps3, Xbox 360, or a steam controller.
PROS
1.The configuration menu has a lot of options to choose from to help make the game feel more comfortable not just to you, but to your computer as well.
2.The game starts off with a bang by launching you into combat from the get go. The combat and leveling system itself is solid and it is addicting to grind not just your level but also your Eidolons and Magic level as well. There is even a training feature that allows you to gain exp with one person while not playing the game.
3.The story itself is well played and even has adopted some of the cultural references from Final Fantasy XIII. The game does allow you to redo missions while keeping all exp, gil, and items. In between missions the choices are yours to make on who to talk to and what sides quest you will take up. Althow right now the story is pretty straightforward I can tell there is about to be a twist and I just do not know where it will come from and this is why I love Final Fantasy.
4.Other than the "CON" combat is a enjoyable and exciting part of this game. It has tons of options that grow more and more with characters level and with the progression of the story keeping it fresh and lemon scented even after 20+ hours of playtime.

While I have never played the original Shadow Warrior, I am familiar with its setting and some gameplay footage. I am extremely glad that the borderline racist protagonist was remade without the accent and cringeworthy stereotypes.
Shadow Warrior is not a great game. You go through levels, pressing buttons to unlock doors or destroy magical seals in order to move forward. In between all of this, you shoot predictable waves of demons or turn to your trusty sword when you run low on ammo. Fairly basic and rather unoriginal. Level design, while diversified, is at times lackluster and uninspired. When you find the same ammo-crates and closets in every level ranging from random house in random village to mountain fortress of solitude, things get a bit dull. Good thing they didn't put those closets in the shadow realm as well.
What makes the game shine is the combat mechanics, especially the swordfighting. While in the early stages, you are best advised to keep your distance and deal headshots, using the sword only sparingly, the sword really starts to shine about 2 hours into the game, after you unlock certain special moves. These not only make dealing with hordes of enemies way easier, but are also pretty fun.
Most of the guns, on the other hand, are pretty useless. I relied mainly on the Shotgun (which is borderline useless before the upgrade to 4-barrels) and Crossbow (again, it only really starts to shine after upgrading, after which it becomes a vital weapon for quick kills). They might as well have left out the flamethrower, since it really only seems to make enemies panic without actually dealing significant damage.
What in the beginning looks like your garden variety macho-guy-slaughters-monsters-to-cope-with-inferiority-complex story turns out to be surprisingly deep and enchanting. The cutscenes are artistically rendered and the overall story really develops into something serious about 2/3 into the game. Although I wasn't able to understand every last detail, since some of it is told in-game, I was pleased with the plotline.
A detail that sort of bothers me are the non-Japanese signs one can find in the harbour level that is supposed to take place in Osaka, Japan. I might be wrong about these, but they are either Chinese or just a random selection of Chinese characters. This along with the protagonist's boss' name Mizayaki (which, as far as I know, is not a real Japanese name - it should probably be Miyazaki), I found to be  a bit unsensitive. Then again, it might be some sort of innuendo or joke that I am not aware of.
Overall, I'd rate the game 7/10. It was a fun experience, even while at times being a bit repetitive and dull. Secret-hunters will definitely be satisfied, as well as those who seek a break from generic duck-behind-a-kneehigh-wall shooters.

Gameplay is superb - a fantastic blend of gunplay with over-the-top weaponry, and swordplay with an immensely satisfying array of katana moves. Slaughtering endless hordes of demons never gets old - which is good since it's pretty much all you'll be doing.
The game ALSO has an amazing sense of humor - Lo Wang fully embraces the hilarity that comes from his last name, and has a multitude of hilarious one-liners in combat. His partner, Hoji, is funny, too - and the two play off each other very well.
The story is... alright, I suppose; it lost me at a couple points but I caught up by the time I hit the ending, which was fairly hard-hitting, in a way that didn't clash with the game's aforementioned light-hearted side. The soundtrack is excellent - worth shelling out for the Special Edition.
If I have a couple gripes, one would be that the scoring system for each fight is very hard to impress; I could slaughter the demons in a minute, be extremely varied in how I get my kills, or manage to get through unscathed, and still get a 2/5. Also, the game seems to have some technical issues; on the first computer I played it on, it took me a few months to get it working before I just reinstalled my drivers, and on my second, much better computer, there are still framerate issues and the resolution doesn't fill the entire screen.
Still, this is an amazing game, and is good for scratching any mayhem-itches you might have.

This game is alright. It places a lot of stress on boat exploration. Which is good considering it is the best part of this game. However, running across the rooftops of Rome or Venice is more fun than riding a boat. Naval battles are where your computer will be put to the test. If you have anything lower than the recommended equipment, you'd might as well buy Revalations.
Boats:
Naval battles provide hours of entertainment. There is nothing more fun in an AC game to date. Riding around in the Jackdaw will keep you hooked on this game for a long time. If you like the running across rooftops of older games, however, this game won't suit your fancy. Like Assassin's Creed 3, there are very few giant cities for Edward to run around. But honestly, the boats alone are great enough to merit a purchase.
Gameplay:
There's still no sneak machanic, however, this game doesn't need one. You spend so little time assassinating people that a sneak feature wouldn't really help you. Instead, you get tailing missions (Yeaaaaaah). I never really noticed how many tailing missions you could fit into a game. Now I know: enough to make the story not worth following.
Story:
Ehh... I didn't finish the story, it isn't really that interesting. For me, the game ended when my ship was as overpowered as I felt like making it. Edward is a fine main character, I guess, but Ezio is still better. Heck, you could even argue that Connor is a better main character. Edward is the first assassin in the series whose goals involve money, rather than furthering the assassins and providing order. Which is fine, but that makes him really unrelatable. Overall, the story and main character are both a hit-or-miss.
There are other features to this game, but if you're buying this game for those, you're wasting your money. I give this game an 7.5/10. It's fun, but the tailing missions and lack of things to do (and climb) on solid ground are dissapointing.

Now, let me just start with one fact: This is the best version of Type-0 available.
So, is the port bad? Yeah, but it's playable under good settings, so haters shut up.
Now, I have played and finished Type-0 on the PSP, loved it, bought a PS4 when the game was released, played the first mission, hated it, why? Controls. American controls are X to Confirm, O to Cancel, which also changed battle controls, where Square attacks, and Circle evades, pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t, right? So this PC version lets you change to the Japanese version of controls: Square attacks, X evades, simple thing, but it makes the whole gameplay actually playable.
Some people will say the graphics are♥♥♥♥♥♥for today standards, or that this is a PSP game, well, so is Dissidia, and it's a pretty darm good game, and if graphics are everything, stop playing indies and go back to your Battlefield or Call of Duty. Sure Squenix does bad ports, would love them to make them better, but let's face reality, they will still focus on consoles and only port games to PC, there is a pretty small chance of they actually changing their priority order.
The main criticism at the time of the console releases of Type-0 was that it was a remaster with medium graphics, but priced as a AAA title. That criticism is agreeable, but it's cheaper here on Steam (Not sure how much in USD though).
Anyway, about the game:
It has random battles, but Action RPG gameplay. You need to level up all characters individually, and they all play differently. Sure you will start with Ace and think he is the best, then you use Jack or Deuce and argues that they are too slow, but everyone has a role and their own style, you need to learn how to play with them or at least stick with your favorite. Just like Dark Souls, you can Evade the vast majority of attacks with good timing, making it possible for a Lvl9 Deuce to defeat a lvl 99 Behemoth,
The Magic System lets you customize your magic attacks, from making them spend less MP but being slower to charge or dropping power, or the other way, anyway, it's possible to max everything, but you will need lots of griding, but this also means that thos spells you started with will still be useful at end game time if you upgraded them. Unlike the normal FF system for magic, here the real thing are the shooting method, like Rifle1 , Bomb 1, Shotgun 1 or Missile, the element itself is just that, an element, and Shotgun 2 is not necessarely better than Shotgun 1
Story wise, this is one of the good ones. there is a war between the 4 crystals, one of the Crystals loses the war at the end of the Tutorial level from an "ultima bomb", you control the Class 0 members, the special chosen ones that somehow are able to use Magic in a different way from everyone else, making them stronger. Each one has their own personality and role, but even when they seem to be fighting, they are still good friends. SPOILER ALERT: You will cry with the ending. Yeah, even knowing about a detailed spoiler when I reached there, I still got really surprised.
The game needs at least 2 playthroughs to be finished completely, reason being there are 2 endings related to a choice you make in the final chapter, the second playthrough has what if scenarios (And extra missions), and the 3rd unlocks Gilgamesh for a fight with each member.
It's a pretty long game.

Hack job of a game.
Fist of all, First Person Melee should've died long ago. It is a non workable game mechanic. If you want to make a melee fighting game, it has to be in third person. Otherwise just make it a shooter.
There is a right way to create a difficult game and there is a path of least resistance that is Shadow Warrior. Giving monsters absurd amount of HP does not make for a challenging game in any adult sense of the word. It makes for a boring and frustrating game.
Two obvious problems here:
1) All the miniboss fights feel like chipping away at a slab of granite with a screwdriver. The first time I encountered a miniboss, I even started doubting if I am doing something wrong, because I hit him so many times and the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ isn't dying.
2) All weapons except for katana are essentially useless, no point even upgrading them. Even my all time favorite - the shotgun is miserably ineffective even against basic demons. Why even bother designing them?
3) You don't feel like a badass hero slaying monsters. You feel like an HP miner.
The way to make a challenging game is by forcing player to react, adapt and use precision. Patience, should be the last thing on that list.
Yes, I played it on highest difficulty, as I always do. It's a matter of pride. No, I didn't find it difficult. It found it tedious and irritating. I finally gave up after the game put me in a closed room with two minibosses that can only be damaged from behind, chrage me at ridicilous angles and spam AOE by touching groud with their fist. I killed this pair before in a large room with plenty of obstacles to avoid their charge, and even that took like 30 minutes of constant running around obstacles and waiting to land a single KI strike. But having the same fight in a closed space? WTF am I even supposed to do here? What a waste of time...
The only redeeming value is the fun dialogs.

Gameplay: Shadow Warrior is a FPS game where you slay demons and some humans here and there, but mostly demons. You have a sword and plenty of guns a revolver, smg, crossbow, shotgun, ect. Overall: The game is about 10 hours (17 chapters) the game is definatly amazing, I would buy it on sale though because I got it for a few dollars on the summer sale, and I would say it's not quite worth the full price ($40)  but it's still a great game.

After the mediocre Stronghold 3 and Stronghold Legends, Crusader 2 brings the series back to their roots.
The developers tried to copy the positive aspects of Crusader 1 and improve them with new features.
However, instead of ending up as an improved version of the first Crusader, the game became a much more RTS-like title. which plays much more different than Crusader 1 than I expected.
What the developers did is basically simplified the whole castle building to a state where almost every building makes sense. This gives the game a much more fast-paced gameplay in the Skirmish Mode.
Compared to Crusader 1 or SH2, the units also seem to be better balanced. Spamming Horse Archers or Knights is for example much more difficult than in the previous game(s), because they can now be countered easily by macemen or whirling dervishes.
The whole combat system in general is improved by special abilites the units have. So instead of having useless and useful units like in Crusader 1, the game has offensive and defensive units with their own abilities. This gives armies a certain variety that can also be seen in games like Age of Empires 2.
I also feel like the current AI Lords are way harder to beat than in Crusader 1:
When the Rat is building catapults (so his sieges are not completely useless ;D) and the Wolf builds a stronghold that lets your castle look like a hovel, you know♥♥♥♥♥♥just got serious :D
But despite these aspects the game still has many flaws that need be patched and improved.
The most important would be performance improvement and bug fixing.
On big maps with many opponents the framerate drops under 20fps even on good PCs.
Also knights are sometimes unable to get on their horses or units stop moving entirely.
In terms of balancing there are still some things the developers need to change:
They already lowered the wood cost of woodcutters in previous patches, but there are still some buildings that seem a little bit too expensive, for example the market that becomes unvaluable through its 500 gold price or mills that cost 200 wood each (guys I want my awesome bread empire back :D).
Despite that they need to add some more NPC Lords( Ssssnake plz :D), Units and buildings that are missing ( for example ladders, tunnels, moats, Gardens and voice overs for your peasents).
All in all this game is different from the Stronghold games. It may not feel that much like a complex castle simulator anymore, but more like a well balanced Strategy Game with castle building elements.
Fact is, there aren´t many games today that have this kind of gameplay, so Crusader 2 has a unique gameplay.
Depite its current issues I recommend this game to everyone that likes strategy games and/or the stronghold series, but keep in mind that there are patches coming that may be improving the game that much, that games like Aoe2 or Command and Conquer have a serious competitor.
